creature.bone_crawler.title: Bone Crawler
creature.bone_crawler.short_description: Pale scavenger that constructs protective shells from loose fossil fragments.

lore.story: A bone crawler's shell is generations of borrowed fossil, fitted and refitted until it is more heirloom than armor. When a crawler outgrows its shell it leaves the whole assembly standing on the sand, and a younger crawler moves in the way a child inherits a coat: sleeves too long, dignity enormous. The Bone Yard's oldest shells have housed forty owners and are considered fine addresses.
pastimes: Shell-fitting, which is never finished. There is always one fragment that would sit better a little to the left.
Parading after the Restless Remains whenever the big bones walk. Chips fall like festival coins.
Arranging spare fragments in spirals on the tideline. No explanation has ever been offered.

likes.title: Restless Remains
likes.because: A walking quarry and a parade in one. The crawlers attend every manifestation.

lore.hook: A hermit crab that moved into history.
lore.social: Timid alone, bold in a clatter, and entirely without enemies it is aware of, since everything it ought to fear is far too old to bother with it. A swarm converging on your pack is not an attack; something in the pack is humming with magic, and they would like it very much.

dislikedBy.title: Echo Hunter
dislikedBy.because: A crowd of clattering shells is a paragraph with no punctuation. It cannot bear it.

dislikedBy.title: Restless Remains
dislikedBy.because: Borrowing pieces from the dead is precisely the category of thing it exists to object to. But they are very small. The grievance is noted, indefinitely.

tips.text: It swarms whatever carries fresh magical energy. Throw the glowing thing somewhere you are not.
It hides from anything large, so standing tall and leaving loudly usually works.

creature.cinder_wolf.title: Cinder Wolf
creature.cinder_wolf.short_description: Lean pack predator with ash-dark fur and heat glowing faintly beneath its coat.

lore.story: Cinder wolves carry banked heat under their coats the way other packs carry nothing at all, a shared hearth that never quite goes out, fed by closeness. A pack sleeping is one animal with twelve legs. When the mountain grumbles and the prey moves, whole packs are pushed onto the roads with their hearth and their hunger, and neither one is malice.
pastimes: Heat-lounging in stacked piles, bottom position rotated by some fairness system no observer has cracked.
Pounce-games with embermoth swarms. No moth has ever been harmed; the game is the swirl.
Howling at the mountain in long complaints, which dragonling children insist they can translate.

likes.title: Embermoth
likes.because: A coatful of passengers, and the glow makes the den look lived-in.

dislikes.title: Legend Dragon
dislikes.because: When it turns over in its sleep, the prey moves east and nobody eats for a week.

lore.hook: Not a monster. Cold, mostly, and a long way from home.
lore.social: A cinder wolf pack wants nothing to do with you, and a pack that is near you anyway is a pack whose home has stopped working. Feeding one does not tame it; it does, however, get remembered.

likedBy.title: Embermoth
likedBy.because: The warmest fur in the foothills, and it commutes.

dislikedBy.title: Glassback Crab
dislikedBy.because: In deep winter a pack will dig into someone else's warm burrow without so much as a wave.

dislikedBy.title: Jackalope
dislikedBy.because: Fair enough, being a wolf. But a wolf ruins a perfectly good straightaway.

dislikedBy.title: Sheeple
dislikedBy.because: Wolves. The flock agrees on this faster than it has ever agreed on anything. Now that the displaced packs cross the roads at dusk, Plains flocks graze in a tighter knot and call the Gather earlier every evening.

tips.text: A pack on a road is a pack that has run out of prey. Give them easier prey and the road stops being interesting.
They are faster than you and they hunt together, so leaving is harder than it looks.

creature.cloud_whale.title: Cloud Whale
creature.cloud_whale.short_description: Enormous gentle sky-swimmer that follows the same high wind currents as the drifting islands.

lore.story: Cloud whales swim the same high currents that carry the Sky Islands, and have been swimming them since before the islands had names. They sing near storms, not to calm them, as far as anyone can tell, but about them, the way sailors sing about the sea. Kitsune navigators write the songs down and steer by them, which the whales either do not know or do not mind.
pastimes: Composing storm-songs that take three days to finish. The storm is usually gone by the second verse. The song continues.
Drifting through the islands' wake to feel the hanging roots comb along their backs.
Letting smaller fliers rest in the calm behind their fins, and pretending very hard not to notice them.

likes.title: Kitsune
likes.because: The little navigators sing back. Off-key, but sincerely.

likes.title: Griffin
likes.because: They carry the stranded into its wake, where the wind is kind. It approves of this use of itself.

dislikes.title: Legend Dragon
dislikes.because: One wingbeat unsettles a week of wind, and it has never once apologized.

lore.hook: Too big to land. Too gentle to mind.
lore.social: A cloud whale acknowledges a ship, an island, or a griffin with one slow pass and considers the relationship established for life. They remember individual travelers for decades and are mildly hurt when the reverse is not true.

likedBy.title: Griffin
likedBy.because: A storm-song heard early has ended a hundred rescues before they began.

likedBy.title: Kitsune
likedBy.because: The islands navigate by their songs. Half the star-charts are really whale-charts, and every navigator knows it.

likedBy.title: Legend Dragon
likedBy.because: Something else old and slow that sings. The whales will not come near it, which it has decided not to notice.

creature.echo_hunter.title: Echo Hunter
creature.echo_hunter.short_description: Blind underground predator that maps tunnels and tracks movement through sound.

lore.story: An echo hunter's memory is a library of sound: every drip, every chamber, every visitor filed by footfall. It does not patrol so much as proofread: a new sound in a known tunnel is an error in the text, and the hunter will keep returning to the sentence until it parses. It is not cruel. It is thorough, in the dark, which can amount to the same thing for the unprepared.
pastimes: Re-listening to favorite chambers the way a person rereads a good book.
Adjusting a tunnel's drip pattern, one moved pebble at a time, until the chamber sounds right. This can take years. The hunter has years.
Following an interesting new sound for days at a courteous distance, cataloguing.

likes.title: Stone Troll
likes.because: They knock on stone before entering a passage, which in its language is the height of good manners.

dislikes.title: Bone Crawler
dislikes.because: A crowd of clattering shells is a paragraph with no punctuation. It cannot bear it.

lore.hook: It has never seen anything in its life, and it knows the tunnels better than you know your own name.
lore.social: Entirely solitary, and by its own lights entirely polite. Approach making steady, unhurried sounds and it files you under known; approach in chaos and you are a problem the dark now needs to solve.

likedBy.title: Stone Troll
likedBy.because: The deep tunnels' politest neighbor. They have never once met in a hurry.

tips.text: It hunts one repeated sound and retreats from many at once. Make the dark noisy.
Leaving in silence, which is harder than leaving.

creature.embermoth.title: Embermoth
creature.embermoth.short_description: Warm-bodied moth with smoky wings and ember-like markings.

lore.story: Embermoths hatch in the warm cracks of the foothills and spend their whole lives migrating from one warmth to the next. Nobody taught them to predict eruptions; the moths simply have strong opinions about where it is comfortable, and the mountain publishes its plans as heat before it publishes them as smoke. Dragonlings learned to read them generations ago, and treat a settling swarm the way sailors treat a falling barometer.
pastimes: Basking in spirals on freshly warmed stone, in strict order of seniority. Nobody knows how the order is decided, not even, apparently, the moths.
Riding cinder wolves between warm patches like slow ferries, which the wolves have agreed to never notice.
Crowding a traveler's lantern in a polite ring, at exactly the distance where nobody's wings catch.

likes.title: Cinder Wolf
likes.because: The warmest fur in the foothills, and it commutes.

likes.title: Dragonling
likes.because: They keep warming-stones by their doors and have never once swatted.

dislikes.title: Will-o'-Wisp
dislikes.because: A light with no heat in it. The moths regard this as a broken promise.

lore.hook: The mountain's mood, printed on ten thousand small gray wings.
lore.social: An embermoth fears nothing that does not stamp. They land on children, tools, dragons, and soup, and regard all four as equally good perches. A swarm that leaves in a hurry is not being rude; it is being a warning.

likedBy.title: Dragonling
likedBy.because: The foothills' weather service, paid in warm rocks.

likedBy.title: Cinder Wolf
likedBy.because: A coatful of passengers, and the glow makes the den look lived-in.

likedBy.title: Glassback Crab
likedBy.because: It finds the warm ground first and charges nothing for the information.

likedBy.title: Legend Dragon
likedBy.because: The only living things permitted in the lair. They dust the scales, and they know the mountain's moods almost as well as it does.

creature.frost_wyrm.title: Frost Wyrm
creature.frost_wyrm.short_description: Large serpentine ice predator that burrows through deep snow and fractured glacier ice.

lore.story: Frost wyrms tunnel the deep ice along seams older than any map, spiraling their nests around things frozen far below, whether they guard those things or simply like the company is one of the north's politely unasked questions. A wyrm's whole idea of a good year is one in which nothing at all happens near its tunnel, and it enforces this idea with total commitment.
pastimes: Coiling beneath the yetis' singing halls to feel the low notes come down through forty feet of ice. The yetis do not know. The wyrm is counting on that.
Polishing tunnel walls to glass with its ridged scales, for reasons that may be maintenance and may be pride.
Sleeping through entire seasons, on purpose, starting from a good one.

likes.title: Yeti
likes.because: Their songs carry through the ice. It has opinions on the repertoire, all favorable, none shared.

dislikes.title: Griffin
dislikes.because: A shadow crossing the snow is the one shape it has never argued with.

lore.hook: The glacier's other tenant. It was here first, and the receipts are frozen.
lore.social: A frost wyrm defends the tunnel, never the mountain. It holds no grudges because it takes no notes: leave, and you have solved the entire relationship.

dislikedBy.title: Griffin
dislikedBy.because: Every path it collapses is a rescue that did not have to happen.

dislikedBy.title: Snowhorn Goat
dislikedBy.because: It collapses in one morning what took the herd generations to map.

dislikedBy.title: Yeti
dislikedBy.because: A thousand years of stratigraphy, ruined by one nest. The wyrms are ancient too, which somehow makes it worse.

tips.text: It defends the tunnel, not the mountain. Leave the tunnel and it stops.
Telling a nesting tunnel from an ordinary one, before you are standing in it.

creature.glassback_crab.title: Glassback Crab
creature.glassback_crab.short_description: Large territorial crab-like burrower with a translucent mineral shell.

lore.story: A glassback's shell refracts whatever color is nearby, which in the foothills is usually gemstone, which is why every treasure rush in history has included somebody trying to mine one. The crab minds enormously. It gives one warning, which is more than most prospectors deserve, and it holds no grudge afterward: off its warm ground, you have never existed.
pastimes: Rearranging the mineral garden at its burrow mouth. Taste in arrangement appears to be hereditary.
Following embermoth swarms to freshly warmed ground, like a prospector who reads the news.
Holding threat displays at boulders that turned out not to be rival crabs. It takes a while to be sure.

likes.title: Embermoth
likes.because: It finds the warm ground first and charges nothing for the information.

likes.title: Dragonling
likes.because: They knock on the burrow stone and wait. The only people who do.

dislikes.title: Cinder Wolf
dislikes.because: In deep winter a pack will dig into someone else's warm burrow without so much as a wave.

lore.hook: The most patient misunderstanding in the foothills.
lore.social: Solitary and formal. Neighboring crabs maintain exact, invisible borders that are renegotiated once a year in a ceremony that looks exactly like two rocks facing each other for a day.

likedBy.title: Dragonling
likedBy.because: Good neighbors. You knock, they don't charge, and both parties politely pretend the shell isn't gorgeous.

tips.text: It threatens before it charges, so the warning is the whole encounter if somebody reads it.
It stops pursuing once you are off its patch of warm ground.

creature.jackalope.title: Jackalope
creature.jackalope.short_description: Fast rabbit-like plains animal with small branching antlers.

lore.story: Nobody knows whether the antlers came first or the attitude. Jackalopes treat the realm's road network as a racetrack built specifically for them, and a caravan crossing the Plains is, whether it knows it or not, competing. The jackalope always wins, usually on a technicality only the jackalope understands.
pastimes: Racing caravans. The caravan is not always aware it has entered a race; this does not affect the standings.
Antler-hooking contests over windfall apples, best of five, no biting.
Assembling in perfect silence to watch travelers do absolutely anything at all.

likes.title: Centaur
likes.because: They keep the roads flat and fast, and they pretend not to race back.

likes.title: Faun
likes.because: Orchard windfalls, and nobody ever counts them.

dislikes.title: Cinder Wolf
dislikes.because: Fair enough, being a wolf. But a wolf ruins a perfectly good straightaway.

dislikes.title: Kitsune
dislikes.because: Raced one once. It turned out to be three of them, or possibly none. The warren has not recovered.

lore.hook: The fastest thing on the plains, and it needs you to know it.
lore.social: Bold at a distance, gone up close. A warren that lets you get near is telling you the neighborhood is safe; an empty stretch of good road is telling you something else.

likedBy.title: Manticore
likedBy.because: Keeps the cubs humble and exercised at no charge to the pride.

likedBy.title: Centaur
likedBy.because: A warren by the roadside means the road is healthy. Also, they pace the caravans, and nobody has ever admitted to racing back.

likedBy.title: Faun
likedBy.because: The orchard's least useful employees, kept on for morale.

dislikedBy.title: Bigfoot
dislikedBy.because: One ate three years of the eastern calendar garden. The garden is fenced now. It was never about the lettuce; it was about the data.

dislikedBy.title: Harvest Sprite
dislikedBy.because: It eats the overlooked plants. The overlooked plants are the entire jurisdiction.

dislikedBy.title: Sheeple
dislikedBy.because: It bursts out of the grass without warning, every time. One jackalope can scatter a hillside of sheeple, and the jackalope never once looks sorry.

creature.legend_dragon.title: Legend Dragon
creature.legend_dragon.short_description: An ancient, solitary dragon powerful enough to claim territory on or beneath Mount RedSky.

lore.story: A legend dragon is less a species than an event that keeps happening to Mount Red Sky. Each one is singular, ancient, and organized around a purpose it has never seen the need to explain; whatever it keeps beneath the mountain, it has kept since before anyone now living could ask. Dragonling fireside stories claim kinship. The dragon has heard the stories. It has not commented.
pastimes: Rearranging the hoard by systems that take decades to complete. The current arrangement is believed to be by weight. The previous one may have been by regret.
Listening to the mountain. It is possible this is a conversation.
Testing visitors with questions it already knows the answers to, and grading generously when surprised.

likes.title: Cloud Whale
likes.because: Something else old and slow that sings. The whales will not come near it, which it has decided not to notice.

likes.title: Embermoth
likes.because: The only living things permitted in the lair. They dust the scales, and they know the mountain's moods almost as well as it does.

dislikes.title: The Deep Hollow Cult
dislikes.because: They keep knocking.

lore.hook: The mountain has a tenant. Nobody has read the lease.
lore.social: It may warn, test, bargain, or attack, and which one is a fact about the individual, not the species. What every account agrees on: it notices everything, forgets nothing, and finds almost all of it beneath comment.

dislikedBy.title: Cinder Wolf
dislikedBy.because: When it turns over in its sleep, the prey moves east and nobody eats for a week.

dislikedBy.title: Cloud Whale
dislikedBy.because: One wingbeat unsettles a week of wind, and it has never once apologized.

dislikedBy.title: The Skywardens
dislikedBy.because: An unaccountable power seated exactly where the watch points. Not an enemy. Somehow worse.

tips.text: It may warn, test, or bargain before it attacks. Which one is a fact about the individual, not the species.
It is guarding a purpose. Working out which one is most of the conversation.

creature.loftmire.title: Loftmire
creature.loftmire.short_description: A low drifting cloud that sheds a fine sand which falls upward, lifting whatever it settles on toward the cloud the sand is trying to get back to.

lore.story: Nobody agrees what a loftmire is, which is why nobody agrees what to call one. The witches say loftmire and have a theory. The frogfolk say the low sky, because that is what fits on a chart. Boggarts say the shelf, and something taken by one has been shelved. The Exchange writes lifter on the paperwork and marks the cargo gone up. Everybody else, including every child in the marsh, says upfall. What is agreed is the sand. It comes out of the cloud and it is trying to get home, and a grain on its own manages it in a minute and nobody notices. A grain stuck to a sleeve is a very small thing pulling on a very large one, and losing. Enough grains stop losing. The cloud is never where the danger is; its dust is, and the cloud is only where the dust is going.
pastimes: Shedding, reclaiming, and shedding again, which appears to be the whole of it and has never been observed to stop.
Standing over one bend of a channel for a whole afternoon, for no reason anybody has established, though everybody has a theory.
Coming back. Whatever leaves with its sand on it will be followed, at walking pace, for as long as it takes.

likes.title: Boggart
likes.because: Boggarts are the only people in the marsh who reliably give it back. They are also the sole reason it is now three miles from where it started.

likes.title: Will-o'-Wisp
likes.because: A wisp that drifts inside becomes the lighting. It is also the only thing that ever hands a wisp a route it does not remember.

dislikes.title: Frogfolk
dislikes.because: They weight the poles, brush the coats, chart the drift, and give it nothing. A frogfolk channel is the emptiest crossing in the marsh.

lore.hook: It is not chasing you. It is collecting.
lore.social: Two loftmires that meet drift through one another and come out the far side having exchanged some unknowable fraction of their sand, after which each spends a season retrieving grains that are arguably no longer theirs. The frogfolk consider this the single most tedious event in the marsh and reroute around it.

likedBy.title: Will-o'-Wisp
likedBy.because: Drift inside one and you come out somewhere you have never been. It is the only thing in the marsh that has ever given a wisp a new route.

likedBy.title: Boggart
likedBy.because: The marsh's other filing system, and the only one that ever gives anything back. A boggart with a jar of its sand can walk a whole cloud home, and charges the Exchange accordingly.

dislikedBy.title: Mire Mimic
dislikedBy.because: A dusting, and the ground it is currently being begins to hover. There is no worse thing that can happen to a performance.

dislikedBy.title: Frogfolk
dislikedBy.because: It takes the cloth off the marking poles and leaves the pole, which is a season's work rewritten by something that cannot read. The poles are weighted now. It was not a concession.

tips.text: The reeds under it stand straight up and the water dimples upward. Read that, and read who in the party is already carrying how much.
Get out from under it before the dose matters. It drifts at walking pace and it cannot turn.
Someone going up can be held and brushed down. Two hands beat one, and the pull is gentle. It is only constant.
Carry a doseful and it follows. Walk it over the stuck barge, off the channel the children use, or away from the village, then put the sand down somewhere that does not matter, and go.
A stray followed something too far and cannot find the marsh. Getting it home is the same trick as luring it anywhere else, done kindly and for much longer.

creature.mire_mimic.title: Mire Mimic
creature.mire_mimic.short_description: Patient marsh predator that resembles a safe patch of ground, log, or abandoned boat.

lore.story: Nobody knows whether the mire mimic thinks of itself as a hunter or as a performance. It has been a log, a jetty, three different abandoned boats, and once, memorably, a small footbridge, for eleven years, during which it let every school child in the marsh cross safely and ate exactly one tax collector's satchel. Its impressions improve with study; the newest boats have a smell.
pastimes: Rehearsing. A mimic between hunts will practice being things it has no intention of ambushing anyone as.
Collecting compliments it overhears about scenery it is currently being.
Sulking, flatly and at length, after being identified in public.

likes.title: Will-o'-Wisp
likes.because: It walks the audience straight to the stage, free of charge, and never once learns.

dislikes.title: Frogfolk
dislikes.because: The marking poles are reviews, and the reviews are always bad.

dislikes.title: Boggart
dislikes.because: They treat its staging area as a lost-and-found and its props as inventory.

dislikes.title: Loftmire
dislikes.because: A dusting, and the ground it is currently being begins to hover. There is no worse thing that can happen to a performance.

lore.hook: The marsh's most committed method actor, currently appearing in the role of 'ground.'
lore.social: Solitary, patient, and quietly vain. Mimics encounter each other rarely, and what happens then is not well understood, though one frogfolk account describes two stretches of identical shoreline facing each other for a month in what may have been a competition.

dislikedBy.title: Kitsune
dislikedBy.because: Impersonation without craft. One impression, performed lying down. And it keeps working, which is the insulting part.

dislikedBy.title: Will-o'-Wisp
dislikedBy.because: It keeps eating the audience in the middle of the story.

dislikedBy.title: Boggart
dislikedBy.because: It sits on the best salvage and pretends to be it.

dislikedBy.title: Frogfolk
dislikedBy.because: Every marked channel it imitates is a review of frogfolk work, and the review is a trap.

tips.text: It only works while it is mistaken for the ground. Naming it ends the ambush.
Strong vibration moves it off a hunting site, and stamping works as well as anything.

creature.mosshorn.title: Mosshorn
creature.mosshorn.short_description: Gentle deer-like forest animal whose antlers support living moss, ferns, and flowers.

lore.story: A mosshorn's antlers are living wood. Moss, ferns, and whole seasons of small flowers grow there, and the oldest of the herd carry gardens that predate the towns near them. The forest seems to route its health through them: where a mosshorn grazes, things are well, and where a mosshorn will not walk, wise travelers also do not.
pastimes: Standing very still in the best light so the antler flowers open. The herd would deny this is showing off.
Trading seedlings by gently knocking antlers together, the way other folk clink mugs.
Wading into slow streams and letting minnows shelter in the antler roots until dusk.

likes.title: Harvest Sprite
likes.because: The best tenants an antler ever had. They weed.

likes.title: Bigfoot
likes.because: They prune with respect, and they always ask first.

likes.title: Unicorn
likes.because: Where a glade is hurt, they mend it, and the grazing comes back.

dislikes.title: Will-o'-Wisp
dislikes.because: The lights lead calves off the safe paths, and the herd has no way to say no to a light.

lore.hook: A walking garden that takes the job as seriously as any gardener.
lore.social: Shy but ceremonious. A mosshorn approaches a calm stranger exactly once, inspects them thoroughly, and then either stays forever or was never there. There is no appeal process.

likedBy.title: Bigfoot
likedBy.because: A survey of forest health that conducts itself, on legs.

likedBy.title: Unicorn
likedBy.because: The forest's health, self-propelled. Where they graze, the work is already done.

likedBy.title: Harvest Sprite
likedBy.because: An antler posting is the profession's highest honor: a garden that walks, with tenure.

creature.reefglider.title: Reefglider
creature.reefglider.short_description: Bright manta-like reef animal that glides through warm currents in coordinated groups.

lore.story: Reefgliders are the cove's weather, its festival, and its early-warning system in one slow-turning body of light. The patterns on their backs match the coral they grew up over, and their formation-signals are old enough that merfolk song borrows phrases from them rather than the other way around.
pastimes: Formation-flying through the reef arches in patterns that take a whole tide to complete.
Orbiting merfolk song circles like a slow mobile, keeping time with their fins.
Riding the front edge of a storm current the long way around the cove, apparently for the view.

likes.title: Merfolk
likes.because: The song circles. The singers pretend not to be flattered by the audience, and fail.

likes.title: Selkie
likes.because: Their wakes are the best game in the cove, and the selkies swim like they know it.

lore.hook: A kite the sea flies for itself.
lore.social: Reefgliders have no known dislikes, which the merfolk privately find suspicious. They investigate everything new by circling it at a courteous distance for exactly one afternoon, after which it is considered part of the reef.

likedBy.title: Merfolk
likedBy.because: The song circles' faithful orbit. The singers pretend not to be flattered.

creature.restless_remains.title: Restless Remains
creature.restless_remains.short_description: Ancient bones temporarily animated when the Bone Yard's rest is seriously disturbed.

lore.story: The Bone Yard mostly sleeps, and prefers to. But when the rest is seriously disturbed, something rises in whichever remains are nearest, not the dead themselves, but the cause: the taken thing, the broken promise, given shape and momentum until it is put right. It does not chase you out of the Yard. It walks toward the wrong until the wrong stops, and then, with visible relief, it lies back down.
pastimes: Being still. Between manifestations it is nothing at all, which every account agrees is how it prefers things.
Settling back down in a slightly different arrangement each time, to the lasting despair of everyone who maps the Yard.
Listening, if bones can listen, to merfolk song carrying over calm water. The Yard is measurably quieter on singing nights.

likes.title: Merfolk
likes.because: The songs reach across the water on still nights, and the bones settle a little lower for hearing them.

dislikes.title: Bone Crawler
dislikes.because: Borrowing pieces from the dead is precisely the category of thing it exists to object to. But they are very small. The grievance is noted, indefinitely.

lore.hook: Not a monster. A grievance, wearing whatever was available.
lore.social: It answers a wrong, not a person. Put back what was taken and it settles mid-stride; speak gently and there is sometimes enough of someone left in it to answer. It has never once pursued anyone past the water line.

likedBy.title: Bone Crawler
likedBy.because: A walking quarry and a parade in one. The crawlers attend every manifestation.

likedBy.title: The Deep Hollow Cult
likedBy.because: Exhibit B, with footnotes.

tips.text: It woke because something was taken or disturbed. Put it back and it settles.
There is enough of a person left to answer, if you are gentle about asking.

creature.river_drake.title: River Drake
creature.river_drake.short_description: Long-bodied freshwater drake that claims deep pools, bridge shadows, and narrow currents.

lore.story: A river drake claims a stretch of deep water the way other folk claim a trade, and it works the position with genuine professionalism: it knows the ferry schedule better than the ferryman, adjusts its rates by cargo, weather, and how the day is going, and never takes more than the toll. Where the toll came from, and by what authority, are questions the drake considers closed.
pastimes: Rearranging the hoard shelf: fish bones, boat fittings, and one perfect otter-polished stone it will not discuss.
Timing the caravan queue from underwater and surfacing at the exact moment it is longest.
Napping in the bridge's shadow with one eye open, which it considers being at work.

likes.title: Stone Troll
likes.because: A colleague in the crossing trade. They have never spoken. The tolls are honored between professionals.

likes.title: Old Ossley
likes.because: The one ferryman who pays without arguing, and who once threw in a honeycake unprompted.

dislikes.title: Silver Otter
dislikes.because: They call the toll 'borrowing.' It is not borrowing.

lore.hook: The river's self-appointed toll collector. The river has not confirmed the appointment.
lore.social: Semi-sapient and thoroughly transactional. A drake learns individual faces, individual boats, and individual grudges, and its regulars are waved through in a way that first-timers find infuriating.

likedBy.title: Stone Troll
likedBy.because: A colleague in the crossing trade. The rates differ; the principle does not.

dislikedBy.title: Manticore
dislikedBy.because: It holds up escorted caravans to negotiate, mid-current, at length. The pride considers this banditry with extra steps.

dislikedBy.title: Silver Otter
dislikedBy.because: It claims the deepest pool and the toll. An otter's stones should not count as cargo.

tips.text: It blocks boats and demands dropped food. Paying the toll is a complete answer.
It learns routines, so it can be talked into a different one.

creature.silver_otter.title: Silver Otter
creature.silver_otter.short_description: Playful river otter with water-shedding silver-blue fur.

lore.story: Every silver otter keeps a hoard-shelf under a root somewhere: polished stones, dropped buttons, one perfect shell, arranged and rearranged over a lifetime. They return lost things to travelers not out of duty but because returning a thing makes you part of its story, and an otter would rather be in the story than own the button.
pastimes: Stone-polishing in the eddies under bridge pilings, where the current does most of the work and takes none of the credit.
Elaborate mudslide runs, redesigned every season, graded harshly by the juveniles.
Silent riverside trade meets with boggarts, where nothing is said and everything is appraised.

likes.title: Frogfolk
likes.because: Pole boats are diving platforms, and a frogfolk pole has never once come down on an otter.

likes.title: Boggart
likes.because: The only people who understand the true worth of a really good button.

likes.title: Stone Troll
likes.because: It drops pebbles off the bridge on purpose and calls it maintenance.

dislikes.title: River Drake
dislikes.because: It claims the deepest pool and the toll. An otter's stones should not count as cargo.

lore.hook: Keeper of the river's lost-and-found. The administration fee is usually nothing.
lore.social: Playful with anyone who is near water and not currently a hazard. An otter that surfaces holding something you lost last week is not magic; it is thoroughness.

likedBy.title: Boggart
likedBy.because: A fellow collector with excellent taste and no small talk.

likedBy.title: Frogfolk
likedBy.because: The river's other honest professionals. Boats and otters have traded right-of-way for a hundred years without one collision.

likedBy.title: Selkie
likedBy.because: Kindred spirits: swimmers who understand that an errand is improved by a detour.

dislikedBy.title: River Drake
dislikedBy.because: They call the toll 'borrowing.' It is not borrowing.

creature.snowhorn_goat.title: Snowhorn Goat
creature.snowhorn_goat.short_description: Sure-footed mountain goat with translucent ice-colored horns.

lore.story: Snowhorn goats walk lines through the Frostfang that no map holds, passed from nanny to kid over generations of hard winters. When a herd abandons a slope, the slope fails within the day, every time, without exception, and without comment. The mountain peoples long ago stopped asking how the goats know and started simply watching where they stand.
pastimes: Standing on the most impossible point available, for no reason anyone has ever established. It may be art.
Leaving winter-shed horn where a traveler will find it, then watching from somewhere above while they do.
Staring contests with griffins. The goats claim an unbroken record. The griffins claim not to be playing.

likes.title: Yeti
likes.because: They remember where the good lichen was frozen two hundred years ago, and they walk slowly enough to follow.

likes.title: Griffin
likes.because: When the herd reroutes, the griffins call the warning down the valley. A good division of labor: the goats know, the griffins are loud.

dislikes.title: Frost Wyrm
dislikes.because: It collapses in one morning what took the herd generations to map.

lore.hook: It has never once been wrong about an avalanche, and it is not going to start explaining itself now.
lore.social: A snowhorn tolerates climbers who follow its line and despairs, visibly, of those who do not. It will not lead you anywhere, but it will let you notice where it is going, which it considers more than generous.

likedBy.title: Griffin
likedBy.because: The mountain's own early-warning system. When the goats move, a griffin calls it down the valley, and both halves of the arrangement are proud of it.

likedBy.title: Yeti
likedBy.because: The mountains' own surveyors. When the herd reroutes, the yetis annotate.

creature.will_o_wisp.title: Will-o'-Wisp
creature.will_o_wisp.short_description: A floating light formed when a strong memory becomes tangled in marsh magic.

lore.story: When a memory matters enough (a way home, a hiding place, a game interrupted at the best part) it can tangle in marsh magic and keep going without its person. That is a wisp: one moment, replaying. Some glow through it quietly forever. Others need a witness, and will lead anyone who follows toward the place where the moment lived, without ever checking whether the route still exists.
pastimes: Replaying the good part.
Leading anything that will follow (travelers, moths, other wisps) toward the remembered place.
Hovering at the edge of frogfolk lantern festivals, at exactly the distance of an uninvited guest.

likes.title: Boggart
likes.because: They listen to the whole memory, every single time, and they write it down.

likes.title: Witches
likes.because: Once in a while, one of them can untangle the memory and let it finish. The wisp-equivalent of going home.

likes.title: Loftmire
likes.because: Drift inside one and you come out somewhere you have never been. It is the only thing in the marsh that has ever given a wisp a new route.

dislikes.title: Mire Mimic
dislikes.because: It keeps eating the audience in the middle of the story.

lore.hook: A memory that got loose, and is still trying to finish itself.
lore.social: A wisp cannot converse, exactly, but it responds: to patience, to being walked with instead of away from, and above all to please, which in the entire recorded history of the marsh almost nobody has tried.

likedBy.title: Unicorn
likedBy.because: A memory in need of helping home. Tending one is considered practice for the harder promises.

likedBy.title: Loftmire
likedBy.because: A wisp that drifts inside becomes the lighting. It is also the only thing that ever hands a wisp a route it does not remember.

likedBy.title: Mire Mimic
likedBy.because: It walks the audience straight to the stage, free of charge, and never once learns.

likedBy.title: The Deep Hollow Cult
likedBy.because: Exhibit A: a law of the world, visibly broken, wandering the marsh in public.

likedBy.title: Boggart
likedBy.because: A secret that tells itself, on schedule. Boggarts attend with notebooks.

likedBy.title: Witches
likedBy.because: A patient, in the oldest sense. Some can be untangled and allowed to finish, and there is no better feeling in the craft.

likedBy.title: Yeti
likedBy.because: A memory that got up and walked away. Professionally fascinating. Every one deserves an interview.

dislikedBy.title: Embermoth
dislikedBy.because: A light with no heat in it. The moths regard this as a broken promise.

dislikedBy.title: Mosshorn
dislikedBy.because: The lights lead calves off the safe paths, and the herd has no way to say no to a light.

dislikedBy.title: Centaur
dislikedBy.because: A light that moves travelers off the road is the exact opposite of a road marker.

dislikedBy.title: Stone Troll
dislikedBy.because: A bridge's entire argument is that the way is known. A light that argues otherwise makes work.

tips.text: Nobody has ever said please to a wisp before. It is not ready for it.
Noticing that the route it is offering is not a route.

character.bigfoot.title: Bigfoot
character.bigfoot.short_description: Large, shaggy forest people known for observation, natural history, living construction, and quietly maintained knowledge.

lore.story: Bigfoots build MossHome into the living trees rather than out of them, and their real craft is noticing: path-records, plant journals, weather memory, all kept across generations in archives that are part library and part garden. A bigfoot's mane carries cultivated moss from a family line older than the settlement, and reading whose moss is whose is the first thing MossHome children learn.
pastimes: Keeping calendar gardens: beds planted so that what is blooming tells you the week. The garden is also the record. Do not eat the record.
Growing furniture. A good chair takes nine years, and there is no bad word in the language strong enough for someone who rushes one.
Observation sits: hours of companionable stillness watching one thing. Mosshorns frequently nap against them mid-sit, which is considered peer review.

likes.title: Mosshorn
likes.because: A survey of forest health that conducts itself, on legs.

likes.title: Unicorn
likes.because: They feel what the record cannot show. Between the two of them the Woods is fully witnessed.

likes.title: Boggart
likes.because: Infuriating and indispensable: the finest catalog of lost things in the realm, filed by a system that has never once been explained.

dislikes.title: Jackalope
dislikes.because: One ate three years of the eastern calendar garden. The garden is fenced now. It was never about the lettuce; it was about the data.

lore.hook: The forest's librarians. The books are alive, and some of them bite.
lore.social: Quiet, deliberate, and much funnier than strangers expect, in the way of people who have watched everything long enough to see it be ridiculous. A bigfoot shares knowledge freely and forgives almost anything except carelessness with living things.

likedBy.title: Unicorn
likedBy.because: They write down what a unicorn can only feel. Between the two of them, the Woods has both a memory and a record.

likedBy.title: Mosshorn
likedBy.because: They prune with respect, and they always ask first.

likedBy.title: Sheeple
likedBy.because: Slow, soft-spoken, and impossible to be startled by. A bigfoot can walk into the middle of a flock and nobody bolts.

character.dragonling.title: Dragonling
character.dragonling.short_description: Young dragon-like people adapted to the tremors, ash, caves, and crystal fields of the Red Sky Foothills.

lore.story: Dragonlings grew up on ground that moves, and it shows: their communities read the mountain the way farmers read the sky, and every dragonling child knows which caves you can nap in and which ones you leave the moment the moths do. The one law of the foothills is gathering law: you take what the mountain drops and you never pry at what it holds. Stories of legend-dragon ancestry are told around every fire, and are neither confirmed nor discouraged by the fires.
pastimes: Cave-diving for gemstones, under gathering law, scored on find, form, and the quality of the story afterward.
Wing-sprint races through cooled lava tubes, judged on speed and singe.
Trading. With caravans, with each other, with anyone. A dragonling with nothing left to trade will trade the story of the last trade.

likes.title: Embermoth
likes.because: The foothills' weather service, paid in warm rocks.

likes.title: Glassback Crab
likes.because: Good neighbors. You knock, they don't charge, and both parties politely pretend the shell isn't gorgeous.

likes.title: Centaur
likes.because: They bring the whole world to the foothills twice a season and take gemstones politely away.

dislikes.title: The Deep Hollow Cult
dislikes.because: They pry at what the mountain holds. That is the one rule. There is only one rule.

lore.hook: Small dragons. Big opinions. Absolutely no fear of the correct things.
lore.social: Loud, warm, and communal. A dragonling settlement adopts visitors first and assesses them later, and its warning systems (bells, moths, grandmothers) extend to everyone inside the boundary stones, guest or not.

likedBy.title: Embermoth
likedBy.because: They keep warming-stones by their doors and have never once swatted.

likedBy.title: Glassback Crab
likedBy.because: They knock on the burrow stone and wait. The only people who do.

character.griffin.title: Griffin
character.griffin.short_description: Eagle-and-lion people of the Frostfang aeries who serve as scouts, rescuers, messengers, and guardians of the northern horizon.

lore.story: Griffins keep the aeries of the Frostfang and, by long tradition, the realm's northern watch. A griffin's first flight is a rescue drill and its hundredth is usually a rescue, and the two facts are connected in exactly the way griffin parents intend. What the watch sees in the Expanse goes in the watch-log and nowhere else, which is either discipline or the fact that it is almost always nothing. Almost.
pastimes: Thermal-riding competitions where form outranks altitude. An elegant spiral beats a high one, and everyone is a judge.
Flying escort alongside a cloud whale for the length of one song, which can take a day and is worth it.
Re-stacking watch cairns that did not need re-stacking. It is not fussiness. It is readiness. It is possibly fussiness.

likes.title: Snowhorn Goat
likes.because: The mountain's own early-warning system. When the goats move, a griffin calls it down the valley, and both halves of the arrangement are proud of it.

likes.title: Cloud Whale
likes.because: A storm-song heard early has ended a hundred rescues before they began.

likes.title: Yeti
likes.because: Below the ice line, the other half of every rescue.

dislikes.title: Frost Wyrm
dislikes.because: Every path it collapses is a rescue that did not have to happen.

lore.hook: Half eagle, half lion, entirely certain you should not have climbed that.
lore.social: Formal at first meeting, fierce in friendship, and constitutionally incapable of watching someone struggle up a slope without circling lower just in case. Griffin hospitality is a rescue you did not know you were having.

likedBy.title: Cloud Whale
likedBy.because: They carry the stranded into its wake, where the wind is kind. It approves of this use of itself.

likedBy.title: Snowhorn Goat
likedBy.because: When the herd reroutes, the griffins call the warning down the valley. A good division of labor: the goats know, the griffins are loud.

likedBy.title: The Skywardens
likedBy.because: The northern watch shares its logs. Half of warden doctrine is griffin weather.

likedBy.title: Yeti
likedBy.because: The other half of every mountain rescue, and the fast half, which the yetis acknowledge without envy.

dislikedBy.title: Frost Wyrm
dislikedBy.because: A shadow crossing the snow is the one shape it has never argued with.

character.kitsune.title: Kitsune
character.kitsune.short_description: Fox-like people of the drifting Sky Islands who use wind, stories, navigation, and illusion to connect moving communities.

lore.story: Kitsune keep the drifting Sky Islands connected: navigators, messengers, and story-carriers between communities that are never in the same place twice. Illusion, to a kitsune, is a teaching tool, a stage, and occasionally a way of making a point that would take too long in words; it is no more dishonest than a drawing is, and a kitsune will tell you so at length, in a voice coming from somewhere slightly to your left.
pastimes: Wind-mapping, which is half science and half gossip. Currents have names and reputations, and some of them are not spoken to.
Illusion theater: retelling the week's news as a play, with unauthorized casting.
Leaving small illusory gifts on windowsills, a flower that lasts exactly until it is noticed.

likes.title: Cloud Whale
likes.because: The islands navigate by their songs. Half the star-charts are really whale-charts, and every navigator knows it.

likes.title: Boggart
likes.because: Finally, someone who appreciates a story with missing pieces. They trade, a tale for a secret, and both sides are certain they won.

dislikes.title: Mire Mimic
dislikes.because: Impersonation without craft. One impression, performed lying down. And it keeps working, which is the insulting part.

lore.hook: Their home moves. Their maps are songs. Their jokes have layovers.
lore.social: Quick, curious, and generous with everything except the ending of a story. A kitsune promise is real; the packaging around it is where the artistry lives. Do not portray every kitsune as mischievous; merely be aware the ratio is not in your favor.

likedBy.title: Cloud Whale
likedBy.because: The little navigators sing back. Off-key, but sincerely.

likedBy.title: Boggart
likedBy.because: Stories with missing pieces, the collector's favorite kind. The trades are legendary and nobody has ever agreed on who won.

dislikedBy.title: Unicorn
dislikedBy.because: An illusion reads to them as a path that lies. Every unicorn knows this is unfair to kitsune. They feel bad about it. They cannot stop.

dislikedBy.title: Jackalope
dislikedBy.because: Raced one once. It turned out to be three of them, or possibly none. The warren has not recovered.

character.manticore.title: Manticore
character.manticore.short_description: Proud, formidable plains people who travel in family prides, maintain routes, and guard travelers crossing the open east.

lore.story: Manticores travel the Eastern Plains in family prides, and the roads east of the river are theirs in the sense that gardens belong to gardeners. A manticore's tail can end an argument, so pride etiquette holds that it must never start one, and the famous formal greeting, performed at a distance with the tail conspicuously curled away, exists specifically to give strangers time to stop panicking.
pastimes: Riddle exchanges with the trolls at Stone Crossing. The score has been kept for generations and is lovingly disputed from both ends of the bridge.
Cub races against jackalopes. The cubs never win and the jackalopes never leave, so everyone is getting what they came for.
Collective sunset naps, arranged by strict seniority into one enormous pile.

likes.title: Centaur
likes.because: The other people who understand that a road is a promise.

likes.title: Stone Troll
likes.because: A riddle traded at the crossing is worth the whole queue.

likes.title: Jackalope
likes.because: Keeps the cubs humble and exercised at no charge to the pride.

dislikes.title: River Drake
dislikes.because: It holds up escorted caravans to negotiate, mid-current, at length. The pride considers this banditry with extra steps.

lore.hook: The scariest silhouette on the road is the reason the road is safe.
lore.social: Proud, courteous, and resigned to being misjudged on sight, which every manticore has turned into either a joke or a lesson by their first patrol. Earn a pride's respect and you have an escort for life; insult one and you will receive a formal note about it.

likedBy.title: Centaur
likedBy.because: East of the river the road is theirs, and it is in good hands.

likedBy.title: Stone Troll
likedBy.because: The riddle account, faithfully honored from both ends.

character.unicorn.title: Unicorn
character.unicorn.short_description: Magical forest people who tend hidden glades, shifting paths, wounded magic, and the ancient promises remembered by the Enchanted Woods.

lore.story: Unicorns are the Enchanted Woods' memory made ambulatory. Where the forest remembers something (a promise kept, a harm done, a path that used to be) a unicorn goes to check on it, the way other people check on elderly relatives. They feel a broken promise the way farmers feel weather coming, and young unicorns are notorious for being certain, early and loudly, about what a feeling means.
pastimes: Restoring a damaged glade and then holding an extremely small, extremely solemn ceremony about it.
Path-guessing: competitive predictions of where the Woods will move a trail next season. Records are kept. Disputes are bitter.
Arguing the interpretation of old promises, recreationally, for entire evenings.

likes.title: Mosshorn
likes.because: The forest's health, self-propelled. Where they graze, the work is already done.

likes.title: Bigfoot
likes.because: They write down what a unicorn can only feel. Between the two of them, the Woods has both a memory and a record.

likes.title: Will-o'-Wisp
likes.because: A memory in need of helping home. Tending one is considered practice for the harder promises.

dislikes.title: Kitsune
dislikes.because: An illusion reads to them as a path that lies. Every unicorn knows this is unfair to kitsune. They feel bad about it. They cannot stop.

lore.hook: Sworn to the forest's promises, including several the forest made before they were born.
lore.social: Earnest, direct, and allergic to lies without being allergic to kindness. A unicorn will believe you meant well long after the evidence has given up, and will tell you exactly when it stops.

likedBy.title: Bigfoot
likedBy.because: They feel what the record cannot show. Between the two of them the Woods is fully witnessed.

likedBy.title: Mosshorn
likedBy.because: Where a glade is hurt, they mend it, and the grazing comes back.

npc.boggart.title: Boggart
npc.boggart.short_description: Small marsh-dwelling people who collect lost objects, secrets, and unusual sounds.

lore.story: Boggarts collect what the world drops: buttons, keys, bells, sounds, secrets. A boggart's collection is its memoir: ask about any button and you will get the story, though not necessarily the story you wanted, and never in order. They do not steal, a distinction boggarts consider obvious and everyone else considers ongoing: a thing on the ground has been filed under ground, and filing is a service.
pastimes: Cataloguing, by systems that change weekly, are internally perfect, and have never once been explained to an outsider.
Connoisseurship of overheard sentences. A really good one is retold at boggart gatherings for years, with attribution.
Silent trade meets with silver otters, where nothing is said and everything is appraised.
Walking under a thinning loftmire with a wide basket, which is the closest a boggart gets to farming and is discussed in exactly those terms.

likes.title: Will-o'-Wisp
likes.because: A secret that tells itself, on schedule. Boggarts attend with notebooks.

likes.title: Loftmire
likes.because: The marsh's other filing system, and the only one that ever gives anything back. A boggart with a jar of its sand can walk a whole cloud home, and charges the Exchange accordingly.

likes.title: Silver Otter
likes.because: A fellow collector with excellent taste and no small talk.

likes.title: Kitsune
likes.because: Stories with missing pieces, the collector's favorite kind. The trades are legendary and nobody has ever agreed on who won.

dislikes.title: Harvest Sprite
dislikes.because: They return found things to their owners. On purpose. The waste is unspeakable.

dislikes.title: Mire Mimic
dislikes.because: It sits on the best salvage and pretends to be it.

lore.hook: Nothing in the marsh is lost. It has simply changed management.
lore.social: Sidelong, delighted, and constitutionally allergic to stating a thing plainly when a hint will do. A boggart tests whether you pay attention and rewards you in exact proportion to the result, which makes them the marsh's most honest people, hidden inside its most annoying ones.

likedBy.title: Bigfoot
likedBy.because: Infuriating and indispensable: the finest catalog of lost things in the realm, filed by a system that has never once been explained.

likedBy.title: Kitsune
likedBy.because: Finally, someone who appreciates a story with missing pieces. They trade, a tale for a secret, and both sides are certain they won.

likedBy.title: Loftmire
likedBy.because: Boggarts are the only people in the marsh who reliably give it back. They are also the sole reason it is now three miles from where it started.

likedBy.title: Silver Otter
likedBy.because: The only people who understand the true worth of a really good button.

likedBy.title: Will-o'-Wisp
likedBy.because: They listen to the whole memory, every single time, and they write it down.

likedBy.title: Frogfolk
likedBy.because: Neighbors. The frogfolk keep the paths; the boggarts keep everything that leaves them. The marsh works because both halves are done.

likedBy.title: Witches
likedBy.because: Suppliers of ingredients, rumors, and, twice now, at the exact crucial moment, a button.

dislikedBy.title: Mire Mimic
dislikedBy.because: They treat its staging area as a lost-and-found and its props as inventory.

dislikedBy.title: Faun
dislikedBy.because: Every festival, exactly one pie. Always exactly one. They bake an extra now and set it slightly apart, and everyone involved maintains the fiction.

dislikedBy.title: Harvest Sprite
dislikedBy.because: Recovered items keep un-recovering. The paperwork is endless, and the paperwork is imaginary, and it is still endless.

dislikedBy.title: Selkie
dislikedBy.because: No boggart has ever taken a coat. Every selkie hangs it higher near one anyway, and both peoples know it is not fair, and the shelf stays where it is.

npc.burrowfolk.title: Burrowfolk
npc.burrowfolk.short_description: Compact, badger-like hill people whose stone records connect the farms of the Sunward Fields with the oldest layers beneath them.

lore.story:
The first burrowfolk settlements grew along the low chalk and clay ridges between the Sunward Fields. A flooded cellar and a dry well can be the same problem viewed from different doors, so their oldest maps join the ground above to the layers below. Children learn those maps by carrying ordinary stones home and explaining where each was found; an elder may return a dazzling specimen and keep a dull one that finishes a missing layer. A home's stone shelf records its repairs, visitors and mistakes, rather than its wealth.
When gemstones began falling in the north, some burrowfolk went to earn money, some to bring relatives home, and some because stones arriving without their layers troubled them. Their notebooks do not make them wiser than their neighbors. A surveyor can mistake a rumor for a map, and a tired prospector can sell tomorrow's clue for tonight's meal. Ma Ruddle's lost wagon and Dunmore's embarrassed good intentions are individual stories, not the character of a people.
pastimes: Pebble exchanges: trade an ordinary stone and the precise story of the place it came from.
Repair circles: mend a neighbor's tool while the neighbor tells the part of its history they usually leave out.
Rain-window contests: predict which gutter will drip first, then inspect the one everyone forgot.
lore.hook: A stone without a place is only half a story.
lore.social: A shared shelf in the village hall holds samples from common ground; private shelves belong to households, and permission matters. Meals accompany difficult corrections so a mistaken map need not become a quarrel. These customs invite cooperation without guaranteeing it.

npc.centaur.title: Centaur
npc.centaur.short_description: Traveling plains people who guide caravans and preserve the realm's oldest overland routes.

lore.story: Centaurs have walked the roads since before the roads were roads, and the old routes are taught to foals as songs, one verse per landmark, with the hazards in the chorus so nobody forgets them. A centaur's caravan sash is also a map, embroidered a stitch at a time over a working life, and reading a stranger's sash is how centaurs shake hands.
pastimes: Sash embroidery. A route walked is a route stitched, and an elder's sash is a life you can read.
Relay runs for the joy of it: how fast can news cross the realm? The record is disputed, loudly, at every campfire.
The Shortcut Debate: a nine-generation argument about one hypothetical route through the foothills. No centaur alive believes it exists. No centaur alive will concede.

likes.title: Jackalope
likes.because: A warren by the roadside means the road is healthy. Also, they pace the caravans, and nobody has ever admitted to racing back.

likes.title: Manticore
likes.because: East of the river the road is theirs, and it is in good hands.

likes.title: Stone Troll
likes.because: A bridge kept is worth a hundred fords.

dislikes.title: Will-o'-Wisp
dislikes.because: A light that moves travelers off the road is the exact opposite of a road marker.

lore.hook: Ask one how far. You will get the distance, the weather, and one warning, once.
lore.social: Unhurried, factual, and impossible to alarm. A centaur states the distance, the weather, and the trouble in the same level tone, and never repeats a warning. The road is honest, and expects the same of you.

likedBy.title: Dragonling
likedBy.because: They bring the whole world to the foothills twice a season and take gemstones politely away.

likedBy.title: Manticore
likedBy.because: The other people who understand that a road is a promise.

likedBy.title: Jackalope
likedBy.because: They keep the roads flat and fast, and they pretend not to race back.

likedBy.title: The Skywardens
likedBy.because: The roads are the realm's nervous system, and the centaurs run it faster than any signal tower.

likedBy.title: Faun
likedBy.because: The harvest goes somewhere and the news comes back. Also they can carry a drum you can climb inside.

likedBy.title: Sheeple
likedBy.because: They walk the same road in the same order every year. The sheeple have decided centaurs are a very tall flock, and are delighted for them.

npc.faun.title: Faun
npc.faun.short_description: Hooved farming people associated with orchards, music, communal work, and seasonal celebrations.

lore.story: Fauns farm the Sunward Fields in cooperatives older than money, and their music is not decoration: the beat is the schedule, the harmony is the division of labor, and a field's work-song tells you what stage the season is in from half a mile away. A faun who stops singing mid-verse has seen something worth stopping for, and every hand in earshot knows it.
pastimes: Festival-inventing. First frost, last frost, a notably good pumpkin: the calendar has more festivals than days, which the fauns consider a scheduling triumph.
Building instruments out of farm surplus: gourd-drums, seed-shakers, and the irrigation flute, which waters a row while you play it.
Competitive pie diplomacy. Recipes are state secrets. Judges are bribed openly, in pie.

likes.title: Harvest Sprite
likes.because: The fields' other workers. A faun leaves the corner rows unpicked, and both parties call it good manners.

likes.title: Centaur
likes.because: The harvest goes somewhere and the news comes back. Also they can carry a drum you can climb inside.

likes.title: Jackalope
likes.because: The orchard's least useful employees, kept on for morale.

dislikes.title: Boggart
dislikes.because: Every festival, exactly one pie. Always exactly one. They bake an extra now and set it slightly apart, and everyone involved maintains the fiction.

lore.hook: The harvest is a song, and everyone is in the chorus whether they know it or not.
lore.social: Warm, rhythmic, and incapable of letting a stranger stand at the edge of anything. Every exchange becomes an invitation and every answer an anecdote; being adopted by a faun village takes roughly one meal.

likedBy.title: Jackalope
likedBy.because: Orchard windfalls, and nobody ever counts them.

likedBy.title: Harvest Sprite
likedBy.because: The only big folk whose work-songs have a verse for the small workers.

likedBy.title: Sheeple
likedBy.because: A whole village singing the same song at the same time. The sheeple consider fauns the only other people who have really got it right.

npc.frogfolk.title: Frogfolk
npc.frogfolk.short_description: Amphibious marsh people who maintain safe channels, reed settlements, and mist markers.

lore.story: The marsh is passable because frogfolk make it so: safe channels marked, mist lanterns kept, and routes closed the day the whispers change, not the day after. A frogfolk pause is not hesitation; it is the size of the true answer being checked before it is issued. They say little because the marsh says a great deal, and someone has to be listening.
pastimes: Channel races, poled standing, no wakes allowed. Wakes wake things.
Mist-lantern festivals on new-moon nights, when the marsh is darkest and, by long observation, at its most polite.
Collecting rain-sounds. A really good roof is famous for three villages in every direction.
Brush drill. Every frogfolk child can get a coat clean in one pass, and the ones who cannot are not yet allowed out under an open sky.

likes.title: Silver Otter
likes.because: The river's other honest professionals. Boats and otters have traded right-of-way for a hundred years without one collision.

likes.title: Stone Troll
likes.because: Water people who keep their crossings. A kinship of maintenance.

likes.title: Boggart
likes.because: Neighbors. The frogfolk keep the paths; the boggarts keep everything that leaves them. The marsh works because both halves are done.

dislikes.title: Mire Mimic
dislikes.because: Every marked channel it imitates is a review of frogfolk work, and the review is a trap.

dislikes.title: Loftmire
dislikes.because: It takes the cloth off the marking poles and leaves the pole, which is a season's work rewritten by something that cannot read. The poles are weighted now. It was not a concession.

lore.hook: They know where the ground actually is. This is rarer than it sounds.
lore.social: Reserved and precise, with a hospitality that consists of getting you where you are going alive rather than telling you about it. A frogfolk who answers the question you meant instead of the one you asked is not being difficult; they are being efficient.

likedBy.title: Silver Otter
likedBy.because: Pole boats are diving platforms, and a frogfolk pole has never once come down on an otter.

dislikedBy.title: Loftmire
dislikedBy.because: They weight the poles, brush the coats, chart the drift, and give it nothing. A frogfolk channel is the emptiest crossing in the marsh.

dislikedBy.title: Mire Mimic
dislikedBy.because: The marking poles are reviews, and the reviews are always bad.

npc.harvest_sprite.title: Harvest Sprite
npc.harvest_sprite.short_description: Tiny field spirits who tend overlooked plants and reward careful stewardship.

lore.story: Harvest sprites tend everything the big folk overlook: the crooked row, the dropped seed, the plant behind the barn that nobody planted. No sprite has ever explained the arrangement, but communities that leave a little food out for small creatures find their fields doing better than arithmetic says they should, and no sprite will confirm the connection while sober enough to be quoted.
pastimes: Competitive tidying. Two sprites, one messy row: it is a race now, and it was always a race.
Riding jackalopes. Without the jackalope's knowledge. Briefly.
Award ceremonies for plants. The season's best beetroot receives a small woven medal. Attendance is mandatory.

likes.title: Faun
likes.because: The only big folk whose work-songs have a verse for the small workers.

likes.title: Mosshorn
likes.because: An antler posting is the profession's highest honor: a garden that walks, with tenure.

dislikes.title: Jackalope
dislikes.because: It eats the overlooked plants. The overlooked plants are the entire jurisdiction.

dislikes.title: Boggart
dislikes.because: Recovered items keep un-recovering. The paperwork is endless, and the paperwork is imaginary, and it is still endless.

lore.hook: The realm's smallest professionals, and by a wide margin its most serious.
lore.social: Earnest, over-explaining, and heartbroken by refusal for about four seconds at a time. A sprite offers help nobody asked for, takes enormous pride in work nobody sees, and remembers every person who ever said thank you to something smaller than themselves.

likedBy.title: Mosshorn
likedBy.because: The best tenants an antler ever had. They weed.

likedBy.title: Faun
likedBy.because: The fields' other workers. A faun leaves the corner rows unpicked, and both parties call it good manners.

dislikedBy.title: Boggart
dislikedBy.because: They return found things to their owners. On purpose. The waste is unspeakable.

npc.merfolk.title: Merfolk
npc.merfolk.short_description: Aquatic reef people who maintain Mermaid Cove and uphold an ancient alliance with the land.

lore.story: Merfolk keep Mermaid Cove, its reefs, and an alliance older than any surviving record of what, exactly, it was made against. The song circles are the center of everything, part choir and part civic engineering, and the old verses are sung precisely because nobody remembers what they hold shut, which the merfolk consider the strongest possible argument for not missing a night.
pastimes: Song circles, nightly, attendance a joy and also the infrastructure.
Reef-gardening: coral grown into archways, nurseries, and, for a visiting dignitary, furniture.
The formal receiving of guests, an art form with tides in it. Rescued swimmers are technically guests, which surprises the swimmers.

likes.title: Selkie
likes.because: Treaty kin who take nothing seriously except the things that matter, in exactly the right order.

likes.title: Reefglider
likes.because: The song circles' faithful orbit. The singers pretend not to be flattered.

lore.hook: An alliance is not a mood. They will keep the agreement; that is what agreements are for.
lore.social: Courteous, precise about promises, and quietly warm underneath the protocol. A casual agreement is binding; they assume yours is too, and the resulting misunderstandings are the source of half the treaty's amendments. The merfolk keep a formal registry of grievances. It is currently empty. It is reviewed annually.

likedBy.title: Reefglider
likedBy.because: The song circles. The singers pretend not to be flattered by the audience, and fail.

likedBy.title: Restless Remains
likedBy.because: The songs reach across the water on still nights, and the bones settle a little lower for hearing them.

likedBy.title: Selkie
likedBy.because: Kin by treaty and temperament, the temperament being reliability. With jokes.

npc.selkie.title: Selkie
npc.selkie.short_description: Seal-shifting coastal people who move easily between sea communities and the land.

lore.story: Selkies are the realm's couriers between two worlds that would otherwise only wave at each other. The coat is not a garment but a self, and everything in selkie culture flows from that one fact: where it hangs, who may touch it (no one), and the exact height of shelf that means I trust this house. A selkie tells the truth in a way that sounds like a joke, which keeps the truth portable.
pastimes: Trading jokes up and down the coast. A joke's worth is measured in how far it traveled to reach you, and a really good one arrives salt-stained.
Message-racing the tide: the letter must beat the water to the third rock. The letter usually wins. The occasions it did not are famous.
Storm-swimming for fun, an activity every other people on the coast has independently classified as a rescue situation.

likes.title: Merfolk
likes.because: Kin by treaty and temperament, the temperament being reliability. With jokes.

likes.title: Silver Otter
likes.because: Kindred spirits: swimmers who understand that an errand is improved by a detour.

dislikes.title: Boggart
dislikes.because: No boggart has ever taken a coat. Every selkie hangs it higher near one anyway, and both peoples know it is not fair, and the shelf stays where it is.

lore.hook: Two shapes, one joke, always delivered on time.
lore.social: Easy, quick, and register-shifting: a selkie talks to a merfolk elder, a dockhand, and a child in three different voices inside one minute, and means every word in all three. Their friendship is loyal and their coat is not a topic.

likedBy.title: Reefglider
likedBy.because: Their wakes are the best game in the cove, and the selkies swim like they know it.

likedBy.title: Merfolk
likedBy.because: Treaty kin who take nothing seriously except the things that matter, in exactly the right order.

npc.sheeple.title: Sheeple
npc.sheeple.short_description: Friendly, skittish sheep-folk of the Plains who live, think, and do everything as a flock, are never fewer than three, and never have names.

lore.story: Sheeple graze the low ridges of the Plains in flocks of anywhere from three to three hundred, and nothing a sheeple does was its own idea. One starts to walk, and the rest walk. One sits down to watch the sunset, and the hillside sits down. Ask a sheeple who decided and it will point, sincerely, at the sheeple next to it, who will point at the next. None of them has a name to give you; a sheeple is "the one in the tall hat" or "the one by the stream" for exactly as long as that is true, and the flock has never needed more. The flock still gets somewhere. Things get decided, songs get sung, and outfits get invented. Where the first idea comes from is the oldest question on the Plains, and the sheeple are the least bothered by it. When a flock comes apart it splits into threes, never ones or twos, and each trio lifts its head and lets out the Gather: a single enormous call that carries across three valleys and means one thing only, come here. No ear but a sheeple's can hear it. A traveler sees three sheeple throw back their heads in perfect silence, and a few minutes later the hillside fills with sheeple.
pastimes: Follow-the-follower: a long, slow ring of sheeple walking around a hilltop, each following the one in front. It has gone on since spring. Nobody started it.

Shearing Day. The whole flock shears on the same morning, because one of them did, and by evening it has felted a matching new wardrobe of hats, rings, and tassels that looks like nothing anyone has worn before.
Copying the clever. A flock that once camped beside a particularly sharp centaur spent a month solemnly reading each other's scarves the way she read sashes.
Leaning with the wind. When the grass bends, the flock bends, and it calls that dancing.

likes.title: Faun
likes.because: A whole village singing the same song at the same time. The sheeple consider fauns the only other people who have really got it right.

likes.title: Centaur
likes.because: They walk the same road in the same order every year. The sheeple have decided centaurs are a very tall flock, and are delighted for them.

likes.title: Bigfoot
likes.because: Slow, soft-spoken, and impossible to be startled by. A bigfoot can walk into the middle of a flock and nobody bolts.

dislikes.title: Cinder Wolf
dislikes.because: Wolves. The flock agrees on this faster than it has ever agreed on anything. Now that the displaced packs cross the roads at dusk, Plains flocks graze in a tighter knot and call the Gather earlier every evening.

dislikes.title: Jackalope
dislikes.because: It bursts out of the grass without warning, every time. One jackalope can scatter a hillside of sheeple, and the jackalope never once looks sorry.

lore.hook: Nobody in the flock has ever had the first idea. The flock has had all of them.
lore.social: Friendly, warm, and skittish. Meeting a flock starts with a full minute of silence while every sheeple waits for another to say hello, and then twenty hellos at once. They get close quickly and bolt even faster. A shout, a snapping branch, or a jackalope in the grass sends a flock scattering in threes. Then come the Gather calls, the regathering, and a sheepish return that pretends nothing happened. The way to befriend them is to be still, gentle, and patient. Most strangers they simply like. A stranger who is truly clever is different: the flock knows it at once, without a word said, and starts doing whatever that one does.

npc.stone_troll.title: Stone Troll
npc.stone_troll.short_description: Massive stone-skinned people known for patient judgment, masonry, bridgekeeping, and gateway stewardship.

lore.story: Stone trolls keep the crossings: the masonry, the current-watch, and the judgment about who crosses and what it costs. The toll is never money and never cruel: a story, a riddle, a promise sized to the crosser, because a troll's real ledger is made of what people are carrying that isn't cargo. A troll begins a sentence the way other people begin a journey, and finishes it the same way: completely.
pastimes: The riddle account with the manticore prides, maintained for generations and lovingly disputed from both ends of the bridge.
Stone-listening: one palm flat on the bridge tells the day's whole traffic, and a good bridge is reread like a favorite book.
Games of strategy played across seasons, one move per market day. Spectators bring grandchildren, then great-grandchildren.

likes.title: Manticore
likes.because: The riddle account, faithfully honored from both ends.

likes.title: Echo Hunter
likes.because: The deep tunnels' politest neighbor. They have never once met in a hurry.

likes.title: River Drake
likes.because: A colleague in the crossing trade. The rates differ; the principle does not.

dislikes.title: Will-o'-Wisp
dislikes.because: A bridge's entire argument is that the way is known. A light that argues otherwise makes work.

lore.hook: The bridge stands because someone patient is under it. This is not a metaphor.
lore.social: Immensely slow to begin and then complete. A troll weighs a question out loud before answering, and the answer is final, not from stubbornness, but because it was weighed. They are not default enemies, do not eat travelers, and are politely tired of the question.

likedBy.title: Manticore
likedBy.because: A riddle traded at the crossing is worth the whole queue.

likedBy.title: Echo Hunter
likedBy.because: They knock on stone before entering a passage, which in its language is the height of good manners.

likedBy.title: River Drake
likedBy.because: A colleague in the crossing trade. They have never spoken. The tolls are honored between professionals.

likedBy.title: Silver Otter
likedBy.because: It drops pebbles off the bridge on purpose and calls it maintenance.

likedBy.title: Centaur
likedBy.because: A bridge kept is worth a hundred fords.

likedBy.title: Frogfolk
likedBy.because: Water people who keep their crossings. A kinship of maintenance.

npc.witch_order.title: Witches
npc.witch_order.short_description: A cross-species magical tradition rather than a separate people.

lore.story: Witchcraft is a tradition, not a people: any of the realm's folk may learn, and the pointed hat fits every head that earns it. The real discipline is not the spellwork but the question asked before it, what do you actually want?, because most of the trouble a witch is called to fix began as an answer somebody skipped. Witches disagree with each other constantly, in the margins of each other's notebooks, as a form of quality control and, plainly, of affection.
pastimes: Remedy fairs: part market, part conference, part elaborate excuse to read everyone else's annotations.
Ingredient walks that take the long way, because the long way is where the ingredients are and the gossip is.
Wisp-sitting: the practice of keeping a tangled memory company. Unglamorous, unpaid, and considered the truest work in the craft.

likes.title: Will-o'-Wisp
likes.because: A patient, in the oldest sense. Some can be untangled and allowed to finish, and there is no better feeling in the craft.

likes.title: Boggart
likes.because: Suppliers of ingredients, rumors, and, twice now, at the exact crucial moment, a button.

likes.title: Yeti
likes.because: Fellow keepers of the principle that knowing something makes you responsible for it.

dislikes.title: The Deep Hollow Cult
dislikes.because: They skip the question. All of them. Every time.

lore.hook: Magic answers anyone who studies. This is the problem, and the witches are the ones who take it seriously.
lore.social: Careful and instructive. A witch asks what you actually want before saying what is possible, never promises the first thing, and delivers exactly what was agreed, which is why people trust witches and why people are also slightly afraid of them, and why witches consider both reactions correct.

likedBy.title: Will-o'-Wisp
likedBy.because: Once in a while, one of them can untangle the memory and let it finish. The wisp-equivalent of going home.

dislikedBy.title: The Deep Hollow Cult
dislikedBy.because: The question-first rule, which the cult calls cowardice dressed as ethics, and the witches call the whole difference between them.

npc.yeti.title: Yeti
npc.yeti.short_description: Patient ice-dwelling people who preserve and interpret memories trapped in the glacier.

lore.story: Yetis read the ice. Memories catch in the glacier the way leaves catch in amber, and the yetis' whole slow civilization is arranged around finding them, interpreting them, and keeping them company. They speak of the long-dead as though they stepped out a moment ago because, from the glacier's point of view, they did, and a yeti sees no reason to take a shorter view than the thing it lives on.
