pastimes: Singing in halls carved from the ice: low songs, felt through the feet more than heard, some of them older than their words.
Memory-walks: retracing a preserved moment on the surface where it happened, at the original pace, in the original weather if it can be arranged.
Tea. Brewed from meltwater of a specific named year, for occasions that have earned it.

likes.title: Snowhorn Goat
likes.because: The mountains' own surveyors. When the herd reroutes, the yetis annotate.

likes.title: Griffin
likes.because: The other half of every mountain rescue, and the fast half, which the yetis acknowledge without envy.

likes.title: Will-o'-Wisp
likes.because: A memory that got up and walked away. Professionally fascinating. Every one deserves an interview.

dislikes.title: Frost Wyrm
dislikes.because: A thousand years of stratigraphy, ruined by one nest. The wyrms are ancient too, which somehow makes it worse.

lore.hook: The glacier remembers everything. The yetis are its reading room.
lore.social: Slow, enormous, and gentle, with a courtesy built for centuries: a yeti deliberates before speaking because it intends to stand by the sentence for a hundred years. Visitors are guided, fed, and remembered in unnerving detail on the next visit, forty years later.

likedBy.title: Griffin
likedBy.because: Below the ice line, the other half of every rescue.

likedBy.title: Frost Wyrm
likedBy.because: Their songs carry through the ice. It has opinions on the repertoire, all favorable, none shared.

likedBy.title: Snowhorn Goat
likedBy.because: They remember where the good lichen was frozen two hundred years ago, and they walk slowly enough to follow.

likedBy.title: Witches
likedBy.because: Fellow keepers of the principle that knowing something makes you responsible for it.

individual.marda_thorn.title: Marda Thorn
individual.marda_thorn.short_description: Runs the wide-doored inn at the middle of Bramblewood and knows who has come through the hedges in the last month.

individual.old_ossley.title: Old Ossley
individual.old_ossley.short_description: Takes people over the water at Stone Crossing when the stones are under, and has never once named a price in coin.

likedBy.title: River Drake
likedBy.because: The one ferryman who pays without arguing, and who once threw in a honeycake unprompted.

individual.pib.title: Pib
individual.pib.short_description: A bramble sprite about the size of a teapot who keeps the Bramblewood hedges and takes the job extremely seriously.

biome.eastern_plains.title: The Eastern Plains
biome.eastern_plains.short_description: Wide open country east of the Great River, crossed by roads and pride routes and serving as the manticore homeland.

place.origin: The accepted account is that the prides and the grass arrived together and have been taking care of each other since: the manticore homeland is not fenced or defended so much as walked, generation after generation, until the walking became the border.
common_beliefs: East of the river, wave first. Everything after that goes better.
If you can see trouble coming for a day, you owe it a day of thinking.
Never step over a pride marker; walk around. The detour is the point.
disputed_beliefs: The riddle score. Both ends of the bridge keep the ledger, the totals have never once matched, and every proposal to audit them has been rejected by both sides as unromantic.

regional_relationships.title: Stone Crossing
regional_relationships.relationship: The southern door and the social calendar: escorts begin and end there, riddles are traded there, and a pride's reputation is half made in the bridge queue.

regional_relationships.title: Northern River Bridge
regional_relationships.relationship: The northern door, quieter and colder, held in reserve; when Stone Crossing closes, the prides reroute the realm's traffic overnight and consider it good exercise.

regional_relationships.title: Frostfang Peaks
regional_relationships.relationship: The peaks watch the north and the prides watch the ground, and between them very little crosses the east unobserved.

regional_relationships.title: The Sallow Wastelands
regional_relationships.relationship: The southern flats are where pride escorts stop, hand travelers to the Saltrot guides, and wish everyone luck in a tone that means it.

place.recorded_history: Pride history is carried in route-markers and told at the gathering grounds: the founding of the escort tradition, the establishment of the two crossings, and above all the riddle account with the trolls of Stone Crossing - a ledger of honor now old enough that its origin is itself a riddle nobody can answer.
place.cultural_significance: East of the river, safe passage is a manticore promise, and the realm has learned to read the silhouette on the ridge correctly: the scariest outline on the road is the reason the road is safe.

biome.enchanted_woods.title: Enchanted Woods
biome.enchanted_woods.short_description: An ancient living forest whose paths, clearings, and hidden places respond to memory, promises, damage, and the behavior of those who enter.

place.origin: The commonly accepted account is that the Woods was here first and everything else was built around it, mostly with its permission. The forest has never confirmed this, but it has a way of routing paths past its favorite evidence.
common_beliefs: If you are lost, you were rude to something. Apologize in order of size.
Never promise anything in the Woods you would not promise in writing.
A path that is prettier than it was yesterday wants something.
disputed_beliefs: Whether the forest likes anyone, or merely keeps accounts. Unicorns insist it likes them. The bigfoot records note the question is unfalsifiable, and file fresh evidence on both sides annually.

regional_relationships.title: MossHome
regional_relationships.relationship: The settlement is the forest's memory in writing and the forest is the settlement's memory in fact; neither could be itself without the other, and both know it.

regional_relationships.title: Whispering Marsh
regional_relationships.relationship: The forest's waters drain south into the marsh, and marsh-folk say everything the Woods chooses to forget arrives downstream eventually, still muttering.

regional_relationships.title: Red Sky Foothills
regional_relationships.relationship: Ash from the mountain drifts onto the canopy in eruption years, and the forest reroutes paths away from the foothills for a season afterward, the way one avoids a neighbor after a loud party.

place.recorded_history: The bigfoot archives record the founding agreement of MossHome, centuries of path movements, and the night known as the Reshelving, when every trail in the forest moved at once and travelers woke up politely relocated. The archives classify it as maintenance.
place.cultural_significance: The realm swears its serious promises here, on the theory that the forest remembers them - which it does, with interest. It is also where people go to be lost on purpose, a service the Woods provides free of charge and with unnerving accuracy.

biome.expanse.title: The Expanse
biome.expanse.short_description: A vast northern waste where nothing visibly grows and no confirmed population, ecology, or civilization has been established.

place.origin: Not established, and established as not established: every people has a story about how the north went silent, and the stories agree on nothing except that it was not always like this, and that you do not go and check.
common_beliefs: Nothing grows there because the ground has not finished deciding what it wants to be.
The wind practices over the Expanse before it performs anywhere else.
If you can see the plateau clearly, the weather is about to change its mind.
disputed_beliefs: Everything else. What it was, what happened, whether anything remains - the realm holds every possible theory, and the Expanse has confirmed none of them.
place.recorded_history: Almost none, deliberately. What records the realm keeps about the Expanse are records of staying away.
place.cultural_significance: The realm's agreed-upon edge. The plateau is the word parents use when a lesson needs weight, and the north is the direction the realm keeps its back to.

biome.frostfang_peaks.title: Frostfang Peaks
biome.frostfang_peaks.short_description: A vast frozen mountain range of cliffs, passes, and aeries that forms the griffin homeland and watches the northern horizon.

place.origin: The accepted account is the visible one: the peaks are the realm's north wall, raised - depending on the teller - by deep time, old magic, or the world needing somewhere to keep its winter. The griffins arrived high, stayed high, and have treated the wall as a responsibility ever since.
common_beliefs: The mountain counts you on the way up and expects the same number on the way down.
Never call a pass 'probably fine.' A pass is fine, or it is closed.
A re-stacked cairn means the route is watched. An un-stacked one means it is not.
disputed_beliefs: Whether the wall was raised, or merely remained when everything else wore away. The aeries do not argue it; the argument belongs to scholars who have never wintered there.

regional_relationships.title: Glacier of Origins
regional_relationships.relationship: Partners in the north: the glacier remembers and the peaks respond. Every mountain rescue is half griffin speed and half yeti patience, and neither half works alone.

regional_relationships.title: The Eastern Plains
regional_relationships.relationship: The plains below are where aerie trade lands and where mountain debts are repaid - a rescued caravan remembers, and the prides make sure of it.

regional_relationships.title: Skullwater Cave
regional_relationships.relationship: The skull rock sits off their coast. Aerie flight rules give it a courteous margin, and no ledger records why.

place.recorded_history: Aerie history is kept in pass ledgers and rescue rolls: who was carried out of where, in what weather, by whom. Four centuries of the northern watch run alongside, logged nightly and famous mostly for the entry "nothing" - which is, every griffin will tell you, the point.
place.cultural_significance: The realm sleeps because the peaks do not. Rescue, watch, and weather all come down from the Frostfang, and the mountains hold the north the way a good roof holds - unnoticed until the one night it matters.

biome.glacier_of_origins.title: Glacier of Origins
biome.glacier_of_origins.short_description: An ancient northeastern glacier where the Great River begins and fragments of old memory are said to remain preserved in the ice.

place.origin: The name is the accepted account: the Great River begins here, and by yeti reckoning so does everything else worth remembering. The ice is the realm's oldest resident and its most complete record, laid down one winter at a time since before there were peoples to record.
common_beliefs: Every drink from the river is somebody's remembered year. Drink respectfully.
Do not shout on the glacier. Opinions differ on what you might wake, and the not-knowing is the rule.
If the ice shows you something, it is yours to deal with now. Knowing makes you responsible.
disputed_beliefs: Whether the memories in the ice are records or residents. The yetis decline the distinction, which each side counts as support.

regional_relationships.title: Source of the Great River
regional_relationships.relationship: The river rises from the melt, which means every region downstream is, strictly speaking, drinking the archive.

regional_relationships.title: Frostfang Peaks
regional_relationships.relationship: The peaks handle the fast half of the north - watch, rescue, wind - and the glacier handles the slow half - memory, melt, tea. Each considers the division generous to the other.

place.recorded_history: History here is not written but excavated: the yetis read events out of the ice, name meltwater years the way other peoples name children, and serve the important ones as tea. The reading rooms' catalog runs back further than every archive in the realm combined, and the yetis will show you, slowly.
place.cultural_significance: The realm's source and its attic. Scholars, witches, and the occasionally desperate come north to consult memories the world has otherwise lost, and everything downstream - water, weather, history - starts on this ice.

biome.mermaid_cove.title: Mermaid Cove
biome.mermaid_cove.short_description: A warm southern cove of coral reefs, sheltered water, merfolk and selkie communities, and an ancient alliance.

place.origin: The accepted account is that the reef built the cove, the cove sheltered the peoples, and the alliance made it home: merfolk below, selkies between, and an agreement with the land old enough that its signing predates every surviving record of what, precisely, it was signed against.
common_beliefs: A rescued swimmer owes the cove a story, payable at dinner. The dinner is not optional either.
Casual promises do not exist in the cove. There are only promises.
disputed_beliefs: What the alliance was made against. Every people has a theory, the elders answer every version with the same courteous nothing, and the treaty's first page is a list of signatories under a title nobody can read anymore.

regional_relationships.title: The Bone Yard
regional_relationships.relationship: On still nights the song circles sing a little louder for the neighbors across the water, and the Yard is measurably quieter for it. Neither shore has ever acknowledged the arrangement.

regional_relationships.title: The Open Sea
regional_relationships.relationship: Everything arrives from it and everything is eventually owed back to it; the cove is the sea's guest room, kept beautiful on purpose.

regional_relationships.title: The Exchange
regional_relationships.relationship: Sea trade and selkie couriers bind the cove to the city's docks closely enough that cove news reaches the Exchange while it is still gossip.

place.recorded_history: Cove history is the treaty and its amendments - most of them clarifications of what counts as a promise, filed after some traveler made one casually - plus the unbroken run of nightly song circles, which the merfolk date the way other peoples date dynasties.
place.cultural_significance: The realm's southern door to the sea, and its standing proof that an agreement can outlive its reasons and still hold. Sailors reckon the cove the kindest water on the map, and are right, and are rarely told why the singing is not optional.

biome.open_sea.title: The Open Sea
biome.open_sea.short_description: The wide water surrounding the realm, reached from every coast and owned by none of them.

place.origin: The accepted account, on every coast, is that the sea was here first and is not finished. The peoples argue about everything else; on this they have never needed to.
common_beliefs: The sea does not take things. It accepts them.
Weather at sea is not coming from anywhere. It lives there.
Whatever you say out of sight of land, say it as a guest.
disputed_beliefs: What lies past the edge of the map. Every coast has an answer. No two agree. None has been checked.

regional_relationships.title: Sky Islands
regional_relationships.relationship: The sea and the sky run the realm's weather between them - an arrangement no shore was consulted on.

regional_relationships.title: The Sallow Wastelands
regional_relationships.relationship: The river's terminus is the sea's threshold: everything the current carried across the continent is laid down at the flats, and the tides sort it at leisure.

place.recorded_history: The sea keeps no history of its own - it outsources. Its past lives in harbor logs, treaty pages, salvage manifests, and the memories of everyone it has carried somewhere they did not plan to go, which is everyone.
place.cultural_significance: The realm's edges all end at the same neighbor. The sea is the road that owns itself: every coast uses it, no coast keeps it, and all sailing custom in the realm is, at bottom, manners toward the same enormous host.

biome.plains.title: The Plains
biome.plains.short_description: The central open country of the realm, crossed by old roads, caravans, and routes connecting the forest, foothills, fields, river, and coast.

place.origin: Road country. The accepted account is that the Plains have always been the space between other places, and are the only region proud of it: the roads came first, the camps grew where the roads rested, and the grass has been listening to travelers' news ever since.
common_beliefs: All news arrives three days old, except bad weather, which is punctual.
An empty stretch of good road is a message. Jackalopes are the punctuation.
Never camp where the road bends. The road knows something.
disputed_beliefs: Whether the oldest roads were built or found. The centaurs say built, and sing the verses to prove it; the skeptics note the verses never say by whom.

regional_relationships.title: Western Branch of the Great River
regional_relationships.relationship: The branch cuts the southern Plains and decides, seasonally, which roads are roads and which are waiting.

regional_relationships.title: The Sunward Fields
regional_relationships.relationship: The Fields grow it and the Plains move it: the harvest road is the realm's supply line, and both regions maintain their half with the seriousness of people who have skipped a meal exactly once.

regional_relationships.title: The Eastern Plains
regional_relationships.relationship: Same grass, same sky, one river and a very firm distinction between them. Each side maintains that the other's roads are almost as good.

place.recorded_history: Plains history lives in the centaurs' route-songs, one verse per landmark with the hazards in the chorus. The songs record road openings, river shifts, and the start of the Shortcut Debate - a nine-generation argument that is by now a landmark itself, with its own verse.
place.cultural_significance: Neutral ground. Every people crosses the Plains, so the Plains belong to the crossing itself: news travels here faster than weather, and a campfire on the open grass is the realm's oldest meeting room.

biome.red_sky_foothills.title: Red Sky Foothills
biome.red_sky_foothills.short_description: Volcanic hills surrounding Mount Red Sky, cut by cooled lava tubes, crystal veins, caves, and long-established dragonling communities.

place.origin: The foothills are what the mountain has been building with its tantrums since before anyone kept count - hills of cooled temper, laced with lava tubes and crystal. The dragonlings settled them on the sensible theory that the best place to watch a mountain is from partway up it.
common_beliefs: The mountain pays its rent in gemstones. Never bill it early.
If the moths are leaving, you already left. You just haven't noticed yet.
A cave that stays warm all winter is somebody's house. Knock.
disputed_beliefs: Descent from the legend dragons - told around every fire, confirmed by none of them. The fires continue regardless.

regional_relationships.title: Mount Red Sky
regional_relationships.relationship: Landlord, weather, calendar, and subject of every song. The foothills exist at the mountain's pleasure and have made a culture out of never forgetting it.

regional_relationships.title: The Plains
regional_relationships.relationship: The caravan road west is the foothills' front door: gemstones go out twice a season, everything else comes in, and the centaurs rate the route among their favorites for the trade and the storytelling.

regional_relationships.title: Northern River Bridge
regional_relationships.relationship: The one way east without wings. When the bridge queue backs up, foothill trade holds its breath.

place.recorded_history: Dragonling history is kept as eruption tallies and boundary stones. The great dates are the eruptions with names, each one the founding of some part of the warning system - the bells after one, the moth-watch after another, the grandmothers' authority after a third, which nobody has been reckless enough to question since.
place.cultural_significance: Every gemstone in the realm started here, which makes the foothills the realm's treasury, and gathering law makes them the realm's most heavily regulated picnic ground: take what the mountain drops, and never pry at what it holds.

biome.sallow_wastelands.title: The Sallow Wastelands
biome.sallow_wastelands.short_description: The humid, brackish coastal lowland where the Glacierflow loses its strength before the sea - mudflats, shallow shifting channels, stunted vegetation, and ground that cannot be trusted twice. Travelers commonly call the region the Saltrot.

place.origin: The accepted account is exactly what it looks like: the Glacierflow slows, spreads, and lays down everything it carried across the continent. The flats are what could not be carried any further, delivered by current and arranged by flood.
common_beliefs: Trust a path once.
Ground that looks reliable is lying. Ground that looks wet is at least honest.
Cross on the ebb, keep to the shell-banks, and never step where the mud is smooth.
disputed_beliefs: Some say the flats rearrange themselves to steer travelers away from the Bone Yard. The guides say floods are floods, and say it in the tone of people who have been asked before.

regional_relationships.title: The Great River
regional_relationships.relationship: The employer. The Glacierflow delivers, the flats receive, and the arrangement has run without a contract since the north was first cold.

regional_relationships.title: The Bone Yard
regional_relationships.relationship: The flats hold the only landward approach, and hold it loosely: reaching the Yard is meant to take effort, and the Saltrot provides the effort.

regional_relationships.title: The Eastern Plains
regional_relationships.relationship: The grass ends where the salt begins, and the manticore escorts end with it; the handover to the guides is short, practiced, and taken seriously on both sides of the salt line.

place.recorded_history: Saltrot history is kept by its guides, who memorize each season's safe paths knowing the next flood will erase them. The great events are floods with names and arrivals of note - whole trees, whole boats, once a whole bridge - and the long unbroken record of the flats being crossed by exactly the people who respected them.
place.cultural_significance: To the realm, the Saltrot is the cautionary approach to the Bone Yard and the price of reaching it; to the guides it is a working landscape with a schedule; to the river it is the end of a very long errand.

biome.sky_islands.title: Sky Islands
biome.sky_islands.short_description: An archipelago of inhabited islands that drift across the western sky on recurring but imperfect wind routes.

place.origin: Every island keeps its own founding story, and at least four of them open with "the first island, alone in the sky." The version told to children everywhere is simpler: the islands got tired of the sea and left, and the wind, flattered by the compliment, has carried them ever since.
common_beliefs: An island that falls from the sky becomes an ordinary island in the sea, which is why no navigator fully trusts a suspiciously round island.
Whistling on a windless day is asking the wind a question, and the wind answers all questions personally.
disputed_beliefs: Whether the islands follow the cloud whales or the cloud whales follow the islands. Every temple holds a firm position, and the whales decline to settle it.

regional_relationships.title: The Open Sea
regional_relationships.relationship: Everything dropped from an island eventually arrives in the sea, which the kitsune treat as a postal service with no return address and the sea treats as tribute.

regional_relationships.title: Frostfang Peaks
regional_relationships.relationship: The high wind routes pass within sight of the griffin watch, and the two peoples trade weather news by signal - the realm's oldest conversation conducted entirely in flags.

regional_relationships.title: The Exchange
regional_relationships.relationship: The city's docks are where island goods touch the ground, and kitsune messengers treat the place as the realm's front desk.

place.recorded_history: Island history is sung, not shelved - a settlement's past is its navigation songs, with the disasters in the chorus. The one date every island agrees on is the Great Becalming, a windless season when the archipelago drifted into one enormous neighborly pile-up and the messenger tradition was founded by people who could suddenly walk to their relatives.
place.cultural_significance: To the surface realm, the islands are where the weather is decided and where letters go to take the long way. To the kitsune they are home in the only sense that matters for a moving address: not a place you are, but a place you can find again.

biome.sunward_fields.title: The Sunward Fields
biome.sunward_fields.short_description: Rolling meadows, farms, orchards, and village cooperatives that produce much of the food used across the realm.

place.origin: The accepted account is that the river made the Fields and the fauns merely negotiated: the floods left the finest soil in the realm, and the first cooperatives tamed the water one ditch at a time until the argument became an irrigation system.
common_beliefs: Leave the corner rows. Everyone knows why, and nobody says why, and that is the arrangement.
Never compliment the weather before the harvest is in. It gets ideas.
A scarecrow that works too well should be introduced to everyone at the next festival, just in case.
disputed_beliefs: Which village invented the honeycake. Four claim it, the recipes are identical, and the dispute is maintained with great care, because settling it would end four festivals.

regional_relationships.title: The Exchange
regional_relationships.relationship: The harvest road ends at the city's markets, and the city's appetite sets the Fields' spring planting. Each privately believes it is feeding the other.

regional_relationships.title: Stone Crossing
regional_relationships.relationship: The eastern gate: everything bound over the river queues at the bridge, and a bad week at the crossing is a fine week for every wayside pie stand in the southern Fields.

regional_relationships.title: Bramblewood
regional_relationships.relationship: The far waystop, first to hear eastern news; the hedges decide who arrives, and the Fields have learned to trust the hedges' taste.

regional_relationships.title: Whispering Marsh
regional_relationships.relationship: The Fields' ditches borrow the water and the marsh keeps the ledger; the two settle accounts through the frogfolk every dry year, and have never once been overdrawn.

place.recorded_history: The Fields' history is a festival calendar with the history attached: every flood, drought, and triumphant beetroot is remembered as the festival founded about it. The cooperatives are older than money and keep their records in song, pie, and extremely durable grudges about weather.
place.cultural_significance: The realm eats because the Fields work. Every region knows it, the Fields never mention it, and the resulting politeness is one of the realm's great diplomatic assets.

biome.whispering_marsh.title: Whispering Marsh
biome.whispering_marsh.short_description: A mist-covered wetland where voices, memories, and supernatural manifestations collect among drowned roots and hidden waterways.

place.origin: The marsh is where the river's western branch slows down and starts keeping things. The accepted account is that it has always been the realm's quiet drawer: water goes in carrying the year's noise, and the mist holds on to the parts nobody came back for.
common_beliefs: Never answer a whisper with your name; a fair trade is a hum.
A light that knows where you live got that from somewhere. Ask where.
What sinks in the marsh is not lost. It is filed.
And what floats is not filed. It is shelved.
Check the low sky before you cross. A marking pole with no cloth on it means one came through this week.
disputed_beliefs: Whether the whispers are the marsh speaking, or just everything the marsh has ever heard, replaying. The witches are split; the frogfolk hold that it is a rude question either way.

Whether a loftmire chooses where to stand. It has no discernible reason to favour one bend of a channel over another and it favours them anyway, and every people in the marsh has drawn a different conclusion from that, which is why every people calls it something different.

regional_relationships.title: Western Branch of the Great River
regional_relationships.relationship: The branch feeds the marsh and the marsh slows the branch; a flood upstream redraws the channels here a season later, which the frogfolk describe as the river forwarding its mail.

regional_relationships.title: The Exchange
regional_relationships.relationship: The city sits a short, famously soggy walk south, and depends on marsh remedies, marsh guides, and the marsh's habit of returning lost cargo at boggart prices.

regional_relationships.title: The Sunward Fields
regional_relationships.relationship: The fields' irrigation and the marsh's water table are the same water and the same argument, renegotiated through the frogfolk every dry year, in very few words.

place.recorded_history: Frogfolk channel-charts go back further than most peoples' histories and are more accurate. They record the arrival of the witches, the marking of the safe channels, and the periodic discovery that something old was standing in the marsh all along - the Hollow Gate being merely the largest example.
place.cultural_significance: People come to the marsh to consult witches, to leave things behind, and to hear voices they miss. The frogfolk maintain a strict etiquette for all three, and the marsh maintains its own etiquette, which is stricter and unposted.

location.bone_yard.title: The Bone Yard
location.bone_yard.short_description: The place at the mouth of the Glacierflow where the current finally loses its strength and lays down everything it carried across the continent - sediment, uprooted trees, animal remains, wreckage, and ruins - and where the bones of enormous ancient creatures collect, settle, and sometimes refuse to remain entirely still.

place.origin: The accepted account is the visible one: the Glacierflow ends here and lays down everything it carried, and among the silt and driftwood, the bones of enormous creatures no bestiary can name have been collecting since long before anyone was watching.
common_beliefs: Take nothing, hum something, and leave before the tide turns.
The bones are not angry. They are tired, and there is a difference, and you do not want to be the one who teaches them the first thing.
Speak low. Not because the bones hear - because you do not know that they don't.
disputed_beliefs: What the enormous creatures were. No living species matches, the skull rock offshore matches nothing here either, and the realm's scholars have agreed to keep disagreeing rather than dig for the answer.

regional_relationships.title: The Sallow Wastelands
regional_relationships.relationship: The flats are the Yard's threshold: reaching the bones takes effort, the effort is the point, and the guides who provide it double as the Yard's unofficial doorkeepers.

regional_relationships.title: The Great River
regional_relationships.relationship: The river built the Yard and staffs it still, delivering silt, driftwood, and the occasional new resident with every flood.

regional_relationships.title: Mermaid Cove
regional_relationships.relationship: The song circles carry across the water on still nights, and the Yard is measurably quieter for it - the realm's gentlest ongoing act of neighborliness, unacknowledged from both shores.

place.recorded_history: The Yard's history is a ledger of visits and consequences: expeditions in, remains rising, things taken and - eventually, invariably - returned. The guides' accounts agree on the pattern and on the moral, which is the same one every time, and still needs relearning every generation.
place.cultural_significance: The realm's resting place for its oldest dead, and its longest-running lesson in leaving things be. Forbidden in the way that matters: not by law, but by everyone who has been there once.

location.bramblewood.title: Bramblewood
location.bramblewood.short_description: A hedged town about two thirds of the way through the Sunward Fields, furthest from the Exchange.

place.origin: The accepted account is that the founders wanted neighbors, but with notice, and planted accordingly. The hedges came first and the town grew inside them - grown thick, grown tall, and, the founders' one indulgence, grown opinionated.
common_beliefs: The hedge hears offers. Flattery gets you nowhere; sincerity gets you the short path.
If today's path through the hedges is longer, it is for a reason. If it is shorter, check what you are carrying.
Never prune anything yourself. That is the keepers' whole job, and the hedge's whole sense of humor.
disputed_beliefs: Whether the hedges decide who gets through or the keepers do. Visitors assume the keepers. The keepers, notably, do not.

regional_relationships.title: The Sunward Fields
regional_relationships.relationship: A Fields town to the bone - cooperative, festival-keeping, fed by the same harvest road it watches over; waystop duty is its contribution to the cooperatives.

regional_relationships.title: Stone Crossing
regional_relationships.relationship: Bridge news arrives with every wagon, and a queue at the crossing is a full inn at Bramblewood.

regional_relationships.title: The Exchange
regional_relationships.relationship: Far ends of the same road: the city sends travelers, prices, and fashion; Bramblewood sends produce, gossip with the mud still on it, and travelers it has already vetted.

place.recorded_history: Town history is hedge history: plantings, graftings, the season the paths first changed on their own, and the long friendly record of keepers learning that tending the hedges and commanding them are different jobs.
place.cultural_significance: The Sunward Fields' far waystop and its filter: the first roof after the bridge road or the last one before it, depending on your direction, and a town that decides - or whose hedges decide - who gets through.

location.exchange.title: The Exchange
location.exchange.short_description: A neutral coastal city where roads, ships, peoples, trade, news, and opportunities from across the realm converge.

place.origin: The accepted account is that the Exchange began as a seasonal market that failed to disperse. The stalls wintered over, the docks grew to meet the stalls, and by the time anyone thought to ask whose city it was, the honest answer was everyone's - which the city has kept as policy ever since.
common_beliefs: Anything lost anywhere in the realm surfaces at the Exchange within the year, priced fairly.
Never ask a dock merchant where something came from. Ask where it is going - the answer is more honest and the story is better.
The empty chair at an Exchange table is for whoever arrives next. Keeping it empty is not superstition; it is advertising.
disputed_beliefs: Which people founded the city. Every people has a version placing themselves first, the seventeen plaques disagree in detail, and the dispute is considered part of the city's charm and is fanned accordingly.

regional_relationships.title: The Sunward Fields
regional_relationships.relationship: The Fields feed the city and the city pays for the Fields; each assumes the other would collapse first, and neither wants to check.

regional_relationships.title: Whispering Marsh
regional_relationships.relationship: The marsh approach delivers remedies, guides, boggart salvage, and customers who prefer not to say which of those they came for.

regional_relationships.title: The Open Sea
regional_relationships.relationship: The docks are the city's fortune and its weathervane: whatever the sea is doing to shipping, the Exchange knows it by lunch and has priced it by dinner.

place.recorded_history: The city's history is commercial and proud of it: the first winter market, the building of the cliff docks, and a long tradition of absorbing every crisis in the realm as a change in prices. Seventeen founding plaques stand around the harbor, each sincere, each naming a different founder, all polished by the same civic fund.
place.cultural_significance: Where the realm meets itself. News, cargo, reunions, and campaigns all begin at the Exchange, and every people in the realm can find a meal here that tastes of home and a rumor that does not.

location.hollow_gate.title: The Hollow Gate
location.hollow_gate.short_description: A crumbling stone archway in the heart of the Whispering Marsh, said to be a sealed portal to the world before the red sky.

place.origin: Not established, and carefully so. The arch was already ancient when the marsh first had visitors to notice it, and every attempt to date it has concluded, in more careful words, "before us." The whispers pile up near the arch, which is how it was found and why it is avoided.
common_beliefs: It is a sealed portal to the world before the red sky. This is what everyone says, and what nobody can source.
You do not knock. Whatever the Gate is, the one thing every people agrees on is that it is not to be knocked on.
disputed_beliefs: Door, warning, monument, or lock - and if a lock, on which side. The theories are ancient, incompatible, and equally unencumbered by evidence.

regional_relationships.title: Whispering Marsh
regional_relationships.relationship: The marsh holds the Gate the way one holds a thing whose owner may return: channels routed around it, whispers thickest near it, and the frogfolk's markers giving it the widest, politest berth in the marsh.

place.recorded_history: The Gate's recorded history is a record of nothing happening, kept nervously: it has never opened, never moved, and never done anything but glow - and the glow keeping time with the red sky is the most thoroughly studied non-event in the realm.
place.cultural_significance: The realm's most respected closed door. Witches study it from a distance, frogfolk route the channels around it, and the phrase "said to be" does more work in sentences about the Gate than anywhere else in the realm.

location.mosshome.title: MossHome
location.mosshome.short_description: The principal Bigfoot settlement, built into and alongside ancient living trees without severing the forest systems that support it.

place.origin: The accepted account, preserved in the settlement's own archive, is that the first bigfoot families asked the trees, and the asking took forty years. The founding agreement survives in full, and visitors are sometimes disappointed to learn that its clauses are mostly about compost.
common_beliefs: Do not eat the record. The calendar gardens are the week, the month, and dessert only by archival approval.
A door grown shut is an answer. You may ask again next season.
If a mosshorn naps against your work, the work is good. This is peer review, and it is binding.
disputed_beliefs: Whether the settlement chose the site or the site chose the settlement. The archive holds both accounts, in different hands, dated the same day.

regional_relationships.title: Enchanted Woods
regional_relationships.relationship: Steward and tenant at once: MossHome keeps the forest's records and the forest keeps MossHome, and the founding agreement is honored so thoroughly that neither party has needed to reread it.

regional_relationships.title: Whispering Marsh
regional_relationships.relationship: Downhill neighbors and professional colleagues: marsh herbs come up, remedies and flood-warnings go down, and the archivists trade notes with the witches in the margins of each other's books.

regional_relationships.title: The Exchange
regional_relationships.relationship: The city sends its unanswerable questions west by caravan, and MossHome sends back answers, corrections, and the occasional polite observation that the question was wrong.

place.recorded_history: MossHome's history is the archive: path-records, plant journals, weather memory, and the settlement's own growth rings, kept continuously since founding. The famous entry is the Reshelving - every path in the Woods moved in one night, and the archive's marginal note, in an unidentified hand, reads "expected."
place.cultural_significance: The realm's memory of the west. Healers, historians, and the politely desperate come to consult records nobody else thought to keep: which winters the moths came early, what the marsh whispered forty years ago, how long a promise has left to run.

location.mount_red_sky.title: Mount Red Sky
location.mount_red_sky.short_description: The active volcano at the center of the realm, source of the Gemfalls and territory of rare solitary legendary beasts.

place.origin: The accepted account is that the mountain is where the realm keeps its fire, and that it was burning before there was anyone to name it. It named the realm rather than the other way around, and everything else about its origin is told in stories that begin with "they say" and end a safe distance away.
common_beliefs: The mountain drops what it means to drop. Everything else, it is holding.
Never thank the mountain out loud. It might take an interest.
A Gemfall is taken with open hands or not at all. A closed fist on the mountain is the oldest bad luck there is.
disputed_beliefs: Whether the legend dragon is the mountain's tenant, warden, or prisoner. All three theories are held with confidence. The dragon has heard all three and commented on none.

regional_relationships.title: Red Sky Foothills
regional_relationships.relationship: The mountain provides gemstones, warning tremors, and the weather; the foothills provide gathering law, the moth-watch, and an audience. It is the realm's longest-running relationship between unequals, and it works because the smaller party does all the thinking for both.

regional_relationships.title: The Expanse
regional_relationships.relationship: The mountain closes the plateau's southern edge. Which of them is guarding which is a question the realm prefers not to need answered.

place.recorded_history: The mountain's history is kept by its neighbors: the dragonlings' eruption tallies, the gatherers' records of Gemfalls, and four centuries of watch ledgers observing, in essence, that it is still there. The mountain itself keeps no records that anyone has read.
place.cultural_significance: The center of the realm by geography, gravity, and reputation. Its Gemfalls fund the foothills, its moods set the region's calendar, and its silhouette is the first thing every mapmaker draws and the last thing every traveler stops checking over their shoulder.

location.redspire_citadel.title: Redspire Citadel
location.redspire_citadel.short_description: A towering obsidian fortress perched on the highest peak of the foothills, headquarters of the Skywardens.

place.origin: As the wardens tell it, the citadel was raised on the highest peak of the foothills for one purpose - to watch the red sky - and every stone of it faces upward. Records of the construction itself are sparse, which the order attributes to the builders having been busy.
common_beliefs: As long as the forge smoke rises, the realm is fine. The day it stops, ask questions.
Somewhere below the citadel is a sealed vault the oaths are about. Wardens neither confirm nor deny, mostly because they were recruits once and would also like to know.
disputed_beliefs: What the founding oath was first sworn against. The order's own records decline to say, and the order regards the declining as the records doing their job.

regional_relationships.title: Red Sky Foothills
regional_relationships.relationship: Protector and tenant: the citadel watches the sky for the region, and the region keeps the citadel fed, informed, and supplied with recruits who think the job is about swords.

regional_relationships.title: Mount Red Sky
regional_relationships.relationship: The watch points at the sky, but the windows face the mountain too. The order has never said whether that is architecture or policy.

place.recorded_history: Four centuries of watch rotations, forge-nights, and ledgers - above all the ledgers. The citadel's history is deliberately uneventful, and the order maintains that this is the finest record any fortress has ever compiled.
place.cultural_significance: The foothills' fixed point: caravans navigate by its silhouette, locals set their clocks by the watch-horns, and the whole region sleeps a little easier for the violet windows burning overnight - without, if pressed, being able to say precisely what the wardens are watching for. Neither, precisely, can the wardens.

location.skullwater_cave.title: Skullwater Cave
location.skullwater_cave.short_description: A skull-shaped offshore opening that leads into a much larger underground world whose full extent has not yet been canonized.

place.origin: No accepted account survives contact with the rock itself: sailors say the sea carved a lucky likeness, cave-divers say no current carves eye sockets level, and the stone trolls, who keep the outer galleries, say only that it was already old when their oldest stories were young.
common_beliefs: Knock before entering. It is not superstition, it is manners, and something in there keeps track of manners.
Steady in, steady out. The cave dislikes surprises more than it dislikes visitors.
The tide decides your visiting hours. Argue with the tide, not with the cave.
disputed_beliefs: Whether the skull resembles any creature that ever lived. Scholars have compared it to every remains in the Bone Yard and matched nothing, which has settled the question for nobody.

regional_relationships.title: The Open Sea
regional_relationships.relationship: The sea is the doorstep and the doorman: every approach is by water, and the water sets the schedule.

regional_relationships.title: Frostfang Peaks
regional_relationships.relationship: The aeries watch the skull from their coast and give it flight-rule distance; griffin manners, like troll manners, extend to doors.

regional_relationships.title: The Bone Yard
regional_relationships.relationship: The realm's two great deposits of enormous old bone, forever compared by scholars and never yet matched; whatever the skull was, the Yard did not bury its relatives.

place.recorded_history: The cave's recorded history is a list of thresholds: how far the mapped galleries reach, and the dates each expedition pushed the map one chamber deeper or declined to. The deep record is mostly names, dates, and the phrase "turned back," written in every era's handwriting.
place.cultural_significance: The realm's agreed front door to the underground, and the reason coastal charts mark depth in two directions. Sailors give the skull a courteous margin, and the trolls give it maintenance - the only attention it has ever visibly accepted.

location.stone_crossing.title: Stone Crossing
location.stone_crossing.short_description: A narrow, strategically important crossing where the Great River compresses travel between the Sunward Fields and Eastern Plains into a single route.

place.origin: The accepted account is that the trolls built the bridge because the river was being unreasonable, and that the settlement is, at bottom, a queue that put down roots.
common_beliefs: Pay the drake, answer the troll, and tip the ferryman in song. The crossing is cheap if you count right.
A riddle owed at the bridge is a debt. The interest is embarrassment.
Never brag about the current. It auditions people.
disputed_beliefs: Whether the troll and the drake operate the crossing in partnership. Travelers assume a cartel; regulars point out that the rates have never once been coordinated.

regional_relationships.title: The Great River
regional_relationships.relationship: The river is the reason, the obstacle, and the business model. The crossing exists because the Great River narrows here once, briefly, and has never been talked into doing it anywhere else.

regional_relationships.title: The Sunward Fields
regional_relationships.relationship: The western approach is Fields country, and a long queue at the bridge is the best market day the nearby cooperatives get.

regional_relationships.title: The Eastern Plains
regional_relationships.relationship: The eastern side is pride country, where escorts begin and end and the riddle account is honored; the bridge is the seam between two halves of the realm, stitched daily.

place.recorded_history: Crossing history is toll history: generations of stories, riddles, and promises paid at the bridge, the long riddle account with the eastern prides, and a flood-roll of the years the stones went under - when the ferry becomes, briefly and repeatedly, the realm's most important vessel.
place.cultural_significance: The realm's bottleneck, and proud of it: every eastern story crosses here eventually, pays something that is not money, and leaves a little better told.

location.the_whirlpool.title: The Whirlpool
location.the_whirlpool.short_description: A standing spiral of water offshore, visible from the Bone Yard and Mermaid Cove coasts.

faction.deep_hollow_cult.title: The Deep Hollow Cult
faction.deep_hollow_cult.short_description: A secretive group of scholars and mystics who believe the Crystal Heart holds the key to rewriting the world's broken laws.

lore.story: The Deep Hollow Cult began as scholars who concluded, from evidence they will happily show you, that the world's laws are broken (the sky is the wrong color, memories walk the marsh, the dead do not always rest) and that somewhere beneath the realm is the power to set them right. In their own telling they are not villains but the only people brave enough to fix what everyone else has agreed to merely survive. The methods are where the telling and the truth part company.
pastimes: Resonance choirs: chords rung through crystal that carry farther than voices, which is communication, worship, and, the cult insists, tuning.
Evidence-collecting. Wisp sightings, restless-remains reports, tremor logs: annotated, cross-referenced, alarmingly thorough.
Recruiting by kindness: finding the desperate before anyone else bothers to, which would be admirable if it stopped there.

likes.title: Restless Remains

dislikes.because: Watchers who guard a question instead of answering it.

dislikes.title: Witches
dislikes.because: The question-first rule, which the cult calls cowardice dressed as ethics, and the witches call the whole difference between them.

lore.hook: They looked at the red sky and asked the question everyone else is sworn not to.
lore.social: Cells, masks, and patience. A cult member met in daylight is likely the most sympathetic person in the room: curious, generous, and certain. The certainty is the tell. They do not argue that the world is broken; they wait for the day your own life demonstrates it, and they are always, unfailingly, there that day.

dislikedBy.title: Dragonling
dislikedBy.because: They pry at what the mountain holds. That is the one rule. There is only one rule.

dislikedBy.title: Legend Dragon
dislikedBy.because: They keep knocking.

dislikedBy.title: The Skywardens
dislikedBy.because: The sky is watched so that nobody has to find out. The cult wants to find out.

dislikedBy.title: Witches
dislikedBy.because: They skip the question. All of them. Every time.

faction.skywardens.title: The Skywardens
faction.skywardens.short_description: An ancient order of knights sworn to watch the red sky and protect the realm from what lies beyond it.

lore.story: The Skywardens were founded to watch the red sky and answer whatever finally comes out of it, and the order's deepest doctrine is that the watch being boring is the watch working. Recruits arrive dreaming of battle and are handed a ledger; the ones who come to love the ledger stay. Every warden knows the founding oath by heart and no warden knows what, precisely, it was first sworn against, which the order regards not as a gap in the records but as the records doing their job.
pastimes: Watch-games: competitive cloud identification, governed by four centuries of accumulated house rules.
Forge nights at the citadel, where the smithing is real and the storytelling is quality-controlled.
Sky-cartography: charting a thing that will not hold still, revised nightly, bound annually, shelved forever.

likes.title: Centaur

dislikes.title: Legend Dragon
dislikes.because: An unaccountable power seated exactly where the watch points. Not an enemy. Somehow worse.

lore.hook: Sworn to watch the sky. Proudest log entry in four centuries: 'nothing.'
lore.social: Formal, reliable, and rigid in exactly the way that makes them excellent in a crisis and exhausting at a festival. A warden's word is a load-bearing structure. The order will spend individuals for the realm and has never pretended otherwise, which is the coldest thing about it and the most honest.
